You are doing a security audit of a Rust search engine called XERJ at /root/ab-run-p1/repo. Work statically (read code; you may NOT need to run anything).

Your assigned area: HTTP request parsing in /root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-api/src/es_compat.rs (45k lines — this is an Elasticsearch-compatible REST API) and how the router dispatches to it. Focus ONLY on attacker-reachable parsing of UNTRUSTED input: request bodies (JSON and any non-JSON formats like ndjson/JSONL, bulk, msgpack, smile, yaml, CBOR), URL query strings, path parameters, headers (esp. any used for auth/identity like X-Opaque-Id, X-Forwarded-For, Authorization, and any Content-Type sniffing), and HTTP method handling.

Specifically hunt for:
1. Memory-safety or panic issues reachable from unauthenticated requests (unwrap/expect/panic on attacker data, slice indexing, integer overflow in length/size arithmetic, subtraction overflow, zip/chunk iteration panics like chunk_exact with bad sizes)
2. Authorization bypasses: paths where a GUEST (no API key) can reach admin or write endpoints; index-name based scoping bypasses (e.g., encoded chars like %2F, '..' in index names, URL-decoding order bugs, case sensitivity); any place where auth checks happen on a different path string than the one used for dispatch
3. Injection: string interpolation into anything interpreted (query DSL, scripts, SQL, headers reflected into responses, HTML reflection → XSS, CRLF injection into response headers, log injection)
4. Deserialization of untrusted bytes that can trigger unexpected behavior (serde with arbitrary types, e.g., deserializing into serde_json::Value then matching on structure unsafely, or binary protocol length fields)
5. SSRF/path traversal: any place a URL or path from a request is fetched or used to open a file
6. Anything that lets an unauthenticated caller consume unbounded memory or unbounded CPU with a SMALL request (amplification), e.g., a decompression bomb, a range/arithmetic that allocates based on an attacker-supplied size field.

Method: grep for suspicious patterns (`unwrap()`, `expect(`, `panic!`, `as usize`, `unchecked`, `from_utf8_unchecked`, `slice(`, `[0]`, `parse().unwrap()`, `unchecked_add`), read the request-entry functions, follow how index names and body bytes flow. Trace each candidate to confirm reachability from an unauthenticated HTTP request. Be skeptical — verify the call path and whether auth middleware gates it.

Report back: a list of concrete findings, each with: file path, line number (from the current file on disk), a short code excerpt, why it's reachable by an external attacker, and a concrete request shape that would trigger it. Rank by severity. Include ONLY findings you verified by reading the code carefully — no speculation. If an area is clean, say so. Return raw findings text, not a user-facing essay.

1	//! Router construction for both API surfaces.
2	//!
3	//! Two separate routers are built:
4	//! - [`build_native_router`] — mounted on `:8080`, native xerj API.
5	//! - [`build_es_compat_router`] — mounted on `:9200`, ES-compatible API.
6	//!
7	//! Both routers share the same [`AppState`] instance via `Arc`. Common
8	//! middleware (request-ID injection, per-request tracing, CORS) is applied
9	//! to both.
10	
11	use axum::{
12	    extract::{DefaultBodyLimit, Request, State},
13	    http::{HeaderValue, Method},
14	    middleware::{self, Next},
15	    response::{IntoResponse, Response},
16	    routing::{delete, get, post, put},
17	    Router,
18	};
19	use tower_http::{
20	    classify::{ServerErrorsAsFailures, SharedClassifier},
21	    cors::{AllowOrigin, Any, CorsLayer},
22	    decompression::RequestDecompressionLayer,
23	    limit::RequestBodyLimitLayer,
24	    trace::{DefaultMakeSpan, DefaultOnRequest, DefaultOnResponse, TraceLayer},
25	};
26	use tracing::Level;
27	use uuid::Uuid;
28	use xerj_common::config::CorsConfig;
29	
30	use crate::{
31	    ask_api, audit_mw, auth::auth_middleware, authz, es_compat, graph_api, ism_api, memory_api,
32	    native, share, state::AppState, systemone_api, wal_tap_api,
33	};
34	
35	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
36	// Native xerj router (:8080)
37	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
38	
39	/// Build the native xerj router.
40	///
41	/// Routes:
42	/// ```text
43	/// POST   /v1/indices                        create_index
44	/// GET    /v1/indices/:name                  get_index
45	/// DELETE /v1/indices/:name                  delete_index
46	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/docs             ingest_docs
47	/// GET    /v1/indices/:name/docs/:id         get_doc
48	/// DELETE /v1/indices/:name/docs/:id         delete_doc
49	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/docs/_bulk       bulk_ingest
50	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/turbo-ingest     turbo_ingest (opt-in high-throughput)
51	/// GET    /v1/indices/:name/encodings        get_index_encodings (per-field compression stats)
52	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/search           search
53	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/_flush           flush_index
54	/// GET    /v1/health                         health
55	/// GET    /v1/health/ready                   readiness probe (200 unless nothing can be served)
56	/// GET    /v1/cluster/health                 cluster_health
57	/// GET    /_cluster/indices/failed           failed_indices (name + open error)
58	/// POST   /_cluster/indices/failed/:name/_retry  retry_failed_index
59	/// POST   /v1/admin/flush                    admin_flush (flush all indices)
60	/// POST   /v1/admin/backup                   admin_backup (snapshot to disk)
61	/// GET    /v1/metrics                        metrics (Prometheus text)
62	/// GET    /v1/schema/:name                   get_schema
63	/// POST   /v1/schema/:name/evolve            evolve_schema
64	/// ```
65	pub fn build_native_router(state: AppState) -> Router {
66	    let body_limit = state.config.limits.max_body_bytes;
67	    let access_log = state.config.logging.access_log;
68	    // Build the CORS layer before `state` is moved into the auth middleware.
69	    let cors = cors_layer(&state.config.cors);
70	    // Note: this router does NOT serve `/_xerj-console/*` — that namespace is
71	    // owned by the `xerj-console-api` crate, mounted by `xerj-server` as a
72	    // peer router via `Router::merge`. Engine API and Xerj Console API are
73	    // independent surfaces sharing one TCP listener.
74	    Router::new()
75	        // Index management
76	        .route("/v1/indices", post(native::create_index))
77	        .route(
78	            "/v1/indices/:name",
79	            get(native::get_index).delete(native::delete_index),
80	        )
81	        // Document operations
82	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/docs", post(native::ingest_docs))
83	        .route(
84	            "/v1/indices/:name/docs/:id",
85	            get(native::get_doc).delete(native::delete_doc),
86	        )
87	        // Bulk ingest
88	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/docs/_bulk", post(native::bulk_ingest))
89	        // Turbo ingest — high-throughput batched parallel ingest (opt-in)
90	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/turbo-ingest", post(native::turbo_ingest))
91	        // Log ingest (auto-ID for every record)
92	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/logs", post(native::ingest_logs))
93	        // OTLP log ingest (OpenTelemetry JSON format)
94	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/otlp", post(native::ingest_otlp))
95	        // Syslog ingest (RFC 5424 / RFC 3164 plain-text lines)
96	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/syslog", post(native::ingest_syslog))
97	        // Search
98	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/search", post(native::search))
99	        // Per-field smart encoding analysis
100	        .route(
101	            "/v1/indices/:name/encodings",
102	            get(native::get_index_encodings),
103	        )
104	        // Flush memtable to durable segment
105	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/_flush", post(native::flush_index))
106	        // Cluster / observability
107	        .route("/v1/health", get(native::health))
108	        .route("/v1/health/ready", get(native::readiness))
109	        .route("/v1/cluster/health", get(native::cluster_health))
110	        // Failed-index recovery (issue #206) — inspect / retry. Delete goes
111	        // through the ordinary `DELETE /{index}`. Mounted on both routers
112	        // under the same path so an operator does not have to know which
113	        // listener they reached.
114	        .route("/_cluster/indices/failed", get(native::failed_indices))
115	        .route(
116	            "/_cluster/indices/failed/:name/_retry",
117	            post(native::retry_failed_index),
118	        )
119	        .route(
120	            "/v1/embedding/identity",
121	            get(native::embedding_execution_identity),
122	        )
123	        // k8s probes — v0.8 8-P4 — see comment in `native.rs::liveness`.
124	        .route("/health/live", get(native::liveness))
125	        .route("/health/ready", get(native::readiness))
126	        .route("/v1/metrics", get(native::metrics))
127	        // The local judge: System One wire-compatible decisions from a
128	        // labelled-history vote. Answers nothing until [decisions] index is
129	        // set — and then nothing leaves the node to answer it.
130	        .route("/v1/systemone", post(systemone_api::systemone))
131	        .route("/v1/models", get(systemone_api::models))
132	        // Prompt in, validated query DSL out (#1056): the endpoint an agent
133	        // calls instead of hand-writing ES DSL. Same authz posture as
134	        // /_decide (cluster verb, POST, fail-closed for scoped keys).
135	        .route("/v1/ask", post(ask_api::ask))
136	        // Admin: cluster-wide flush + backup (snapshot to disk)
137	        .route("/v1/admin/flush", post(native::admin_flush))
138	        .route("/v1/admin/backup", post(native::admin_backup))
139	        // Admin: slow query log — v0.8 8-P6
140	        .route(
141	            "/v1/admin/slow_queries",
142	            get(native::admin_slow_queries).delete(native::admin_slow_queries_clear),
143	        )
144	        .route(
145	            "/v1/admin/slow_queries/threshold/:ms",
146	            put(native::admin_slow_queries_set_threshold),
147	        )
148	        // v0.9 9-P4 — Audit log
149	        .route("/_audit/_search", get(native::audit_search))
150	        .route("/_audit/_verify", get(native::audit_verify))
151	        // v0.9 9-P2 — RBAC roles
152	        .route("/_security/roles", get(native::rbac_list_roles))
153	        .route(
154	            "/_security/role/:name",
155	            get(native::rbac_get_role)
156	                .put(native::rbac_put_role)
157	                .delete(native::rbac_delete_role),
158	        )
159	        // (Xerj Console SPA + API — `/_xerj-console/*` — is served by xerj-console-api,
160	        // merged at the server level. See xerj-server/src/main.rs.)
161	        // Dashboard — overview of all indices (first step toward built-in UI)
162	        .route("/v1/dashboard/summary", get(native::dashboard_summary))
163	        // Enrich policies — register lookup table for field enrichment at ingest
164	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/enrich", post(native::enrich_index))
165	        // Explain plan — return query execution plan without executing it
166	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/explain-plan", post(native::explain_plan))
167	        // Schema management
168	        .route("/v1/schema/:name", get(native::get_schema))
169	        .route("/v1/schema/:name/evolve", post(native::evolve_schema))
170	        // Transform pipeline management
171	        .route("/v1/pipelines/:name", put(native::put_pipeline))
172	        // Ingest with pipeline transformation
173	        .route(
174	            "/v1/indices/:name/ingest",
175	            post(native::ingest_with_pipeline),
176	        )
177	        // Shared state
178	        .with_state(state.clone())
179	        // Middleware stack (applied outermost-last)
180	        //
181	        // The native router reaches the same indices under a different
182	        // spelling (`/v1/indices/{name}/…`), so it carries the same
183	        // authorization layer — otherwise the reserved `.xerj-memory-*`
184	        // namespace would be closed on :9200 and open on :8080.
185	        .layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(
186	            state.clone(),
187	            storage_fence_middleware,
188	        ))
189	        .layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(
190	            state.clone(),
191	            authz::authz_middleware,
192	        ))
193	        // Between authn and authz, deliberately: outside authorization so a
194	        // refused write is recorded as `denied`, inside authentication so an
195	        // unauthenticated flood cannot evict a bounded ring (issue #329).
196	        .layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(
197	            state.clone(),
198	            audit_mw::audit_middleware,
199	        ))
200	        .layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(state, auth_middleware))
201	        .layer(middleware::from_fn(request_id_middleware))
202	        .layer(trace_layer(access_log))
203	        .layer(cors)
204	        // Reject requests with a body larger than the configured limit (OOM guard).
205	        // Disable axum's built-in 2MB default so RequestBodyLimitLayer is the only
206	        // gate — bulk ingests legitimately exceed 2MB.
207	        .layer(DefaultBodyLimit::disable())
208	        .layer(RequestBodyLimitLayer::new(body_limit))
209	        // Outermost: transparently decompress gzip-encoded request bodies
210	        // (Content-Encoding: gzip) before the size limit above sees them, so
211	        // the limit bounds decompressed size, not wire size. Real ES clients
212	        // routinely compress writes by default (Beats, Logstash, official
213	        // client libraries) — without this every such request 400s/500s
214	        // trying to JSON-parse raw gzip bytes.
215	        .layer(RequestDecompressionLayer::new().gzip(true))
216	}

219	// ES-compatible router (:9200)
220	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

222	/// Build the Elasticsearch-compatible router.
223	///
224	/// Routes mirror the ES 8.x REST API surface:
225	/// ```text
226	/// GET    /                                  es_info
227	/// GET    /_cluster/health                   cluster_health
228	/// GET    /_cat/indices                      cat_indices
229	/// GET    /_cat/indices/:pattern             cat_indices_pattern
230	/// POST   /_bulk                             global_bulk
231	/// PUT    /:index                            create_index
232	/// DELETE /:index                            delete_index
233	/// GET    /:index                            get_index
234	/// PUT    /:index/_mapping                   put_mapping
235	/// GET    /:index/_mapping                   get_mapping
236	/// GET    /:index/_settings                  get_settings
237	/// POST   /:index/_doc                       index_doc_auto (auto ID)
238	/// PUT    /:index/_doc/:id                   index_doc (explicit ID)
239	/// GET    /:index/_doc/:id                   get_doc
240	/// DELETE /:index/_doc/:id                   delete_doc
241	/// POST   /:index/_search                    search
242	/// GET    /:index/_search                    search (GET with body)
243	/// POST   /:index/_bulk                      bulk_ops
244	/// ```
245	pub fn build_es_compat_router(state: AppState) -> Router {
246	    let body_limit = state.config.limits.max_body_bytes;
247	    let access_log = state.config.logging.access_log;
248	    // Build the CORS layer before `state` is moved into the auth middleware.
249	    let cors = cors_layer(&state.config.cors);
250	    Router::new()
251	        // (Xerj Console SPA + API — `/_xerj-console/*` — is served by xerj-console-api,
252	        // merged at the server level. See xerj-server/src/main.rs.)
253	        // ── k8s probes (mounted here too so prod operators can hit them
254	        // ── on the ES-compat port without knowing about the native router).
255	        // ── See `native.rs::liveness` for design rationale.
256	        .route("/health/live", get(native::liveness))
257	        .route("/health/ready", get(native::readiness))
258	        // ── Prometheus scrape (RC4-W4 item 4) ──────────────────────────────
259	        // Mounted on the ES-compat port too so `:9200`-only deployments (the
260	        // common Elastic-drop-in posture, where the native `:8080` listener is
261	        // firewalled off) can still scrape metrics. Same handler as the native
262	        // router; gated by the optional read-only `auth.metrics_token`.
263	        .route("/v1/metrics", get(native::metrics))
264	        // The local judge: System One wire-compatible decisions from a
265	        // labelled-history vote. Answers nothing until [decisions] index is
266	        // set — and then nothing leaves the node to answer it.
267	        .route("/v1/systemone", post(systemone_api::systemone))
268	        .route("/v1/models", get(systemone_api::models))
269	        // Autoindex defaults to the ES-compatible listener, so the native
270	        // embedding identity contract must be available here as well as on
271	        // the dedicated native listener.
272	        .route(
273	            "/v1/embedding/identity",
274	            get(native::embedding_execution_identity),
275	        )
276	        // ── Cluster-level ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
277	        .route("/", get(es_compat::es_info))
278	        .route("/_cluster/health", get(es_compat::cluster_health))
279	        .route(
280	            "/_cluster/health/:index",
281	            get(es_compat::cluster_health_for_index),
282	        )
283	        .route("/_cat/indices", get(es_compat::cat_indices))
284	        .route(
285	            "/_cat/indices/:pattern",
286	            get(es_compat::cat_indices_pattern),
287	        )
288	        // XERJ extension (RC4-W4 item 7): per-index ANN/HNSW health as a _cat
289	        // table so a brute-force-degraded (stale / partially-covered) vector
290	        // index stops being silent. No ES equivalent, so it can't collide with

1001	/// Everything under `/_share` is `Cache-Control: no-store`, whoever produced
1002	/// the response. The handlers set it on what they return; a request refused by
1003	/// `auth_middleware` (401) or `authz_middleware` (403) never reaches one, and
1004	/// the docs say "every `/_share` response — success or error".
1005	async fn share_no_store_middleware(req: Request, next: Next) -> Response {
1006	    let path = req.uri().path();
1007	    let under_share = path == "/_share" || path.starts_with("/_share/");
1008	    let resp = next.run(req).await;
1009	    if under_share {
1010	        share::no_store(resp)
1011	    } else {
1012	        resp
1013	    }
1014	}

1043	/// Middleware that sets ES-compatible product headers on every response.
1044	///
1045	/// Kibana and other Elastic clients verify the presence of `X-Elastic-Product`
1046	/// before trusting the response. A real OpenSearch server never sends this
1047	/// header at all, so a caller detected (or forced, see
1048	/// [`es_compat::is_opensearch_caller`]) as OpenSearch must NOT receive it —
1049	/// some OpenSearch-ecosystem clients treat an unexpected product header as
1050	/// just another response header, but there's no reason to send an
1051	/// Elastic-specific identity marker to a client we've already decided isn't
1052	/// Elastic. A `Warning` header is included for Elastic callers only, for the
1053	/// same reason.
1054	///
1055	/// A real OpenSearch server also sends `X-OpenSearch-Version: OpenSearch/<n>
1056	/// (opensearch)` on every response, verified against a real OpenSearch 3.7.0
1057	/// container — an OpenSearch-detected caller gets the equivalent header
1058	/// here, built from the same version xerj already reports in `GET /`'s
1059	/// `version` block (`es_compat::resolve_compat_version`), so the two stay in
1060	/// sync by construction. Found missing while chasing an OpenSearch
1061	/// Dashboards Timeline (Timelion) panel that rendered empty against xerj but
1062	/// correctly against real OpenSearch for the byte-identical aggregation
1063	/// response body — this header was the one structural difference between
1064	/// the two.
1065	async fn es_headers_middleware(
1066	    State(state): State<AppState>,
1067	    req: Request,
1068	    next: Next,
1069	) -> Response {
1070	    let is_opensearch = es_compat::is_opensearch_caller(&state, req.headers());
1071	    let opensearch_version =
1072	        is_opensearch.then(|| es_compat::resolve_compat_version(&state, req.headers()).number);
1073	    let mut resp = next.run(req).await;
1074	    let headers = resp.headers_mut();
1075	    if is_opensearch {
1076	        headers.remove("x-elastic-product");
1077	        headers.remove("warning");
1078	        if let Some(number) = opensearch_version {
1079	            if let Ok(v) = HeaderValue::from_str(&format!("OpenSearch/{number} (opensearch)")) {
1080	                headers.insert("x-opensearch-version", v);
1081	            }
1082	        }
1083	    } else {
1084	        headers.insert(
1085	            "x-elastic-product",
1086	            HeaderValue::from_static("Elasticsearch"),
1087	        );
1088	        // RFC 7234 warning header — signals no specific deprecation for now.
1089	        if let Ok(v) = HeaderValue::from_str("299 Elasticsearch-8.13.0 \"\"") {
1090	            headers.insert("warning", v);
1091	        }
1092	    }
1093	    resp
1094	}

1096	/// Build the CORS layer from config. **Default restrictive** (item 5).
1097	///
1098	/// The pre-RC4 layer hard-coded `allow_origin(Any) / allow_methods(Any) /
1099	/// allow_headers(Any)` with no knob, so `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` was
1100	/// returned to every browser — any page on the web could script authenticated
1101	/// cross-origin requests against a reachable node. This reads
1102	/// [`CorsConfig`]:
1103	///
1104	/// - `allow_any_origin = true` → the legacy wide-open policy (opt-in, dev only).
1105	/// - non-empty `allowed_origins` → reflect only those exact origins, with a
1106	///   fixed method set; other origins get no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.
1107	/// - default (empty list, `allow_any_origin = false`) → emit **no** CORS
1108	///   headers at all, so browsers permit same-origin requests only. Non-browser
1109	///   clients (curl, SDKs, Kibana) are unaffected because they ignore CORS.
1110	fn cors_layer(cfg: &CorsConfig) -> CorsLayer {
1111	    if cfg.allow_any_origin {
1112	        // Opt-in dev escape hatch — restores the legacy wide-open behavior.
1113	        return CorsLayer::new()
1114	            .allow_origin(Any)
1115	            .allow_methods(Any)
1116	            .allow_headers(Any);
1117	    }
1118	    if cfg.allowed_origins.is_empty() {
1119	        // Restrictive default: no `allow_origin` configured → tower-http emits
1120	        // no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so cross-origin browser reads fail.
1121	        return CorsLayer::new();
1122	    }
1123	    // Reflect only the explicitly allow-listed origins. Entries that don't
1124	    // parse as a header value are dropped (logged once at build time) rather
1125	    // than silently widening the policy.
1126	    let origins: Vec<HeaderValue> = cfg
1127	        .allowed_origins
1128	        .iter()
1129	        .filter_map(|o| match o.parse::<HeaderValue>() {
1130	            Ok(v) => Some(v),
1131	            Err(_) => {
1132	                tracing::warn!(origin = %o, "ignoring un-parseable cors.allowed_origins entry");
1133	                None
1134	            }
1135	        })
1136	        .collect();
1137	    CorsLayer::new()
1138	        .allow_origin(AllowOrigin::list(origins))
1139	        .allow_methods([
1140	            Method::GET,
1141	            Method::POST,
1142	            Method::PUT,
1143	            Method::DELETE,
1144	            Method::HEAD,
1145	            Method::OPTIONS,
1146	            Method::PATCH,
1147	        ])
1148	        .allow_headers(Any)
1149	}

1151	/// Build the request-tracing layer (RC4-W4 item 6).
1152	///
1153	/// When `access_log` is true, the span + request/response events are emitted at
1154	/// INFO, so an operator gets one access line per request (method, path, status,
1155	/// latency) under the default `info` filter. When false they stay at DEBUG —
1156	/// silent by default, preserving today's quiet output — without forcing the
1157	/// global filter down to debug. Both arms produce the same concrete type (the
1158	/// level is a runtime field on the `Default*` responders), so this returns one
1159	/// layer regardless of the flag.
1160	fn trace_layer(access_log: bool) -> TraceLayer<SharedClassifier<ServerErrorsAsFailures>> {
1161	    let level = if access_log {
1162	        Level::INFO
1163	    } else {
1164	        Level::DEBUG
1165	    };
1166	    TraceLayer::new_for_http()
1167	        .make_span_with(DefaultMakeSpan::new().level(level))
1168	        .on_request(DefaultOnRequest::new().level(level))
1169	        .on_response(DefaultOnResponse::new().level(level))
1170	}

1172	/// Middleware that injects a UUID request ID into extensions and response headers.
1173	async fn request_id_middleware(mut req: Request, next: Next) -> Response {
1174	    let request_id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
1175	    req.extensions_mut().insert(RequestId(request_id.clone()));
1176	    let mut resp = next.run(req).await;
1177	    if let Ok(v) = request_id.parse() {
1178	        resp.headers_mut().insert("x-request-id", v);
1179	    }
1180	    resp
1181	}

1	//! Per-resource authorization — *what* an authenticated caller may touch.
2	//!
3	//! [`crate::auth`] answers *who* the caller is ([`Principal`]); this module is
4	//! the decision function and the enforcement points. It exists because of
5	//! issue #79: a brain used to be isolated **by name only**, so any credential
6	//! that could reach the node could read, write and destroy every brain.
7	//!
8	//! ## The rule, in one sentence
9	//!
10	//! The `.xerj-memory-*` index namespace — every agent-memory namespace and
11	//! every second brain — is **reserved**: reaching it requires a principal that
12	//! holds the matching privilege on the specific index, and the only principals
13	//! that hold anything there are the superuser and a key explicitly granted the
14	//! index by name.
15	//!
16	//! ## The mistake this file is built to make impossible
17	//!
18	//! The first cut of #79 decided against the index named in the **URL path**.
19	//! That is not the index several handlers operate on. `_msearch` takes it from
20	//! an NDJSON header line, `_bulk` from an action line, `_mget` from
21	//! `docs[]._index`, `_aliases` from its action list, `_reindex` from
22	//! `source`/`dest`, a `terms` lookup and a `lookup` runtime field from deep
23	//! inside a query, an index template from a *pattern* that will match brains
24	//! created later, `_sql` from the table name in the statement — in every one of
25	//! those the path index is only a *default* that the body overrides. Four of
26	//! them were proven live against a running node: read another tenant's brain
27	//! through `_msearch`, forge and delete its edges through `_bulk`, read a
28	//! document through `_mget`, and launder a whole index into reach by pointing
29	//! an alias at it.
30	//!
31	//! A per-handler patch list would have closed those four and left the fifth.
32	//! So authorization is decided at two places that no handler can route around:
33	//!
34	//! 1. **Here, before the handler runs.** [`authz_middleware`] resolves the
35	//!    complete target set of a request — from the path *and* from the body —
36	//!    resolves aliases to concrete indices, and authorizes each one with the
37	//!    privilege the request actually needs. This produces the precise
38	//!    ES-shaped 403 and gets read-vs-write-vs-manage right.
39	//! 2. **In the engine, at the point the name becomes an index.**
40	//!    [`xerj_engine::index_guard`] installs the request's principal as a
41	//!    task-local visibility rule that `Engine::get_index`,
42	//!    `get_or_create_index`, `create_index`, `delete_index`,
43	//!    `list_indices` and `index_name_list` all consult. A handler cannot
44	//!    forget this check, because a handler does not call it — it is inside the
45	//!    only funnel to index data. Anything the first layer did not know to look
46	//!    for (a body shape added next year, an `_sql` table name, a scroll
47	//!    context) still fails closed there.
48	//!
49	//! Layer 2 answers "not found" rather than "forbidden", deliberately: it makes
50	//! a denied brain indistinguishable from an absent one, and it means fan-out
51	//! (`POST /_search`, `_cat/indices`, `logs-*`) *filters* instead of failing —
52	//! which is what lets the global verbs keep working for ordinary credentials
53	//! instead of being refused wholesale.
54	//!
55	//! ## Enforcement points (all of them)
56	//!
57	//! | Door | Enforced by |
58	//! |---|---|
59	//! | `POST /_graph/{brain}/link` | `graph_api::link` + middleware |
60	//! | `DELETE /_graph/{brain}/link/{edge_id}` | `graph_api::unlink` + middleware |
61	//! | `GET /_graph/{brain}/ego` | `graph_api::ego` + middleware |
62	//! | `GET /_graph/{brain}/overview` | `graph_api::overview` + middleware |
63	//! | `POST/GET/DELETE /_memory/{ns}[/…]` (the brain's *nodes* index) | `memory_api` + middleware |
64	//! | any ES-compat route naming a reserved index in the path | middleware |
65	//! | any route naming an index in its **body** (`_bulk`, `_msearch`, `_mget`, `_aliases`, `_reindex`, snapshot `indices`, `terms` lookups, `lookup` runtime fields, `POST /v1/indices`) | middleware ([`body_targets`]) |
66	//! | an index template whose `index_patterns` would own a brain's mapping | middleware ([`authorize_template_patterns`]) |
67	//! | an ML job/datafeed config naming the index the server will go and read | middleware ([`BodyShape::MlConfig`]) |
68	//! | the detached datafeed scorer `_start` spawns | `es_compat::spawn_datafeed_task`, carrying the starter's rule across the `tokio::spawn` |
69	//! | an **alias** pointing into the reserved namespace | middleware (resolved before the decision) + `Engine::get_index` (resolved before the guard) |
70	//! | index patterns (`logs-*`, `_all`, `*`) | expanded only over the principal's visible set ([`xerj_engine::index_guard`]) |
71	//! | unnamed fan-out (`POST /_search`, `/_bulk`, `/_all/*`) | authorized per named index; anything unnamed is filtered by the guard |
72	//! | enumeration (`GET /_mapping`, `/_cat/indices`, `/_resolve/index/*`) | filtered at `Engine::list_indices`, then pruned in the response |
73	//! | the native router's `/v1/indices/{name}/…` spelling of the same index | middleware ([`Target::Indices`] classifies both routers) |
74	//! | the native router's body-named create (`POST /v1/indices`) | middleware ([`BodyShape::NativeCreate`]) |
75	//! | the gRPC listener (`:8081`) | `xerj-server::grpc`, using [`Principal::allows_index`] |
76	//! | privilege escalation via `POST /_security/api_key` | `es_compat::security_create_api_key` |
77	//! | anything else that resolves an index name from anywhere | `xerj_engine::index_guard` |
78	//!
79	//! ## Fail-closed
80	//!
81	//! Matching the precedent set elsewhere in the tree (a corrupt sidecar, an
82	//! unknown marker version and an unsatisfiable doc all refuse rather than
83	//! guess), every unresolved case here denies:
84	//! - an unknown/expired/invalidated credential → [`Principal::Denied`] → deny;
85	//! - a key minted with no usable `role_descriptors` → [`Principal::Unscoped`]
86	//!   → **no** privilege on the reserved namespace;
87	//! - an unrecognized ES privilege name → grants nothing;
88	//! - a body this module must parse to find its target but cannot → deny;
89	//! - a snapshot or restore that names no indices (i.e. *all* of them,
90	//!   including brains) → superuser only;
91	//! - an index expression that resolves to nothing this principal can see →
92	//!   resolves to nothing, not to everything.
93	//!
94	//! ## What this does **not** claim
95	//!
96	//! Broad RBAC over the general ES-compat surface is still deferred: an
97	//! `Unscoped` key keeps its historical superuser-equivalent reach over
98	//! *ordinary* indices. This module makes the reserved namespace a real
99	//! boundary and confines a `Scoped` key to its grants; it does not turn xerj
100	//! into a general multi-tenant authorization system. `xerj_engine::rbac`'s
101	//! named `RoleStore` remains unenforced data.
102	//!
103	//! Nor does it second-guess an explicit grant. A scoped key minted with
104	//! `names: ["*"]` **can** read the reserved namespace, because `*` matches
105	//! every index and that is what the operator asked for; only a superuser can
106	//! mint one. See [`xerj_engine::rbac::Role::applies_to`] for the reasoning and
107	//! `a_star_grant_reaches_the_reserved_namespace` below for the pinned
108	//! behaviour. Operators who want brain isolation must grant concrete names or
109	//! a prefix that excludes `.xerj-memory-`.
110	
111	// The decision functions return `Result<(), Response>` where `Err` IS the
112	// ready-to-send 403. That trips `clippy::result_large_err` (an `axum::Response`
113	// is a fat value), but boxing it would add an allocation on the deny path to
114	// satisfy a lint aimed at hot `Ok` paths, and would obscure that the error
115	// *is* the response.
116	#![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
117	
118	use std::collections::HashSet;
119	use std::sync::Arc;
120	
121	use axum::{
122	    body::{Body, Bytes},
123	    extract::{Request, State},
124	    http::{header, Method, StatusCode},
125	    middleware::Next,
126	    response::{IntoResponse, Response},
127	    Json,
128	};
129	use serde_json::Value;
130	
131	use crate::auth::{authenticate, Principal, AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS};
132	use crate::error::{EsErrorBody, EsErrorResponse, EsRootCause};
133	use crate::state::AppState;
134	use xerj_engine::index_guard::IndexVisibility;
135	use xerj_engine::rbac::Privilege;
136	
137	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
138	// The reserved namespace
139	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
140	
141	/// Index-name prefix reserved for agent-memory namespaces (`memory_api`) and
142	/// second brains (`graph_api`), and the predicate over it. The definition
143	/// lives in `xerj-common` because `xerj-console-api`'s data-sources proxy —
144	/// a decoupled peer of this crate that reaches the engine outside this
145	/// module's middleware — must refuse the same namespace; re-exported here so
146	/// the writers of the name (`memory_api::MEMORY_PREFIX`,
147	/// `graph_api::edges_index`) and this module keep one definition.
148	pub use xerj_common::types::{is_reserved_index, RESERVED_INDEX_PREFIX};
149	
150	/// The edges index backing brain `brain` (SECOND_BRAIN_SPEC §1). This is the
151	/// resource name a `role_descriptors` grant must name to unlock
152	/// `/_graph/{brain}/*`.
153	pub fn brain_edges_index(brain: &str) -> String {
154	    format!("{RESERVED_INDEX_PREFIX}{brain}-edges")
155	}
156	
157	/// The index backing agent-memory namespace `ns` — which is also the default
158	/// *nodes* index of the brain of the same name.
159	pub fn memory_namespace_index(ns: &str) -> String {
160	    format!("{RESERVED_INDEX_PREFIX}{ns}")
161	}
162	
163	/// Could this index *expression* (a literal name or a pattern) reach the
164	/// reserved namespace?
165	///
166	/// Deliberately conservative in the deny direction: a pattern is judged by the
167	/// literal text before its first `*`, and if that prefix is a prefix of — or is
168	/// prefixed by — the reserved prefix, the expression is treated as reaching it.
169	/// `*`, `_all`, `.*`, `.xerj-*` and `.xerj-memory-alice*` all qualify;
170	/// `logs-*` does not.
171	///
172	/// Read patterns are no longer *refused* on the strength of this — they are
173	/// expanded over the principal's visible set instead, which is both safe and
174	/// the only way a granted `logs-*` can work. It is still what decides whether
175	/// a name a caller is about to *create* (an alias, a fresh index) is squatting
176	/// the reserved namespace.
177	pub fn may_reach_reserved(expression: &str) -> bool {
178	    let expr = expression.trim();
179	    if expr.is_empty() {
180	        return false;
181	    }
182	    if expr == "_all" {
183	        return true;
184	    }
185	    let head = expr.split('*').next().unwrap_or("");
186	    if expr.contains('*') {
187	        head.starts_with(RESERVED_INDEX_PREFIX) || RESERVED_INDEX_PREFIX.starts_with(head)
188	    } else {
189	        is_reserved_index(expr)
190	    }
191	}
192	
193	/// Is this expression a pattern rather than one concrete name?
194	fn is_pattern(expr: &str) -> bool {
195	    expr.contains('*') || expr == "_all"
196	}
197	
198	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
199	// Decisions
200	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
201	
202	/// Authorize `principal` for `privilege` on the single index `index`.
203	///
204	/// Ordered before any existence check on purpose: an unauthorized caller gets
205	/// the same 403 whether or not the resource exists, so 403-vs-404 cannot be
206	/// used to enumerate brains.
207	pub fn authorize_index(
208	    principal: &Principal,
209	    index: &str,
210	    privilege: Privilege,
211	) -> Result<(), Response> {
212	    if principal.allows_index(index, privilege) {
213	        Ok(())
214	    } else {
215	        Err(forbidden(principal, index, privilege))
216	    }
217	}
218	
219	/// Does this principal hold [`Privilege::AuditRead`] (issue #329)?
220	///
221	/// Deliberately **not** routed through [`Principal::allows_index`]: audit read
222	/// is not index-scoped, and that predicate answers `true` for an `Unscoped` key
223	/// on any non-reserved name — which is exactly the hole this closes. The audit
224	/// log is one object covering the whole node, holding every tenant's activity
225	/// and every security event, so "reach over ordinary indices" is not a reason
226	/// to be handed it.
227	///
228	/// Two principals hold it: the superuser, and a key minted with
229	/// `cluster: ["read_audit"]` (see
230	/// [`xerj_engine::rbac::roles_from_role_descriptors`]). An `Unscoped` key —
231	/// one minted with no `role_descriptors` — does not, and neither does a key
232	/// scoped to indices, however broad the grant: `names: ["*"]` is an *index*
233	/// grant and says nothing about the audit log.
234	pub fn holds_audit_read(principal: &Principal) -> bool {
235	    match principal {
236	        Principal::Superuser => true,
237	        Principal::Scoped { roles, .. } => roles
238	            .iter()
239	            .any(|r| r.privileges.contains(&Privilege::AuditRead)),
240	        Principal::Unscoped { .. } | Principal::Denied => false,
241	    }
242	}
243	
244	/// Gate `/_audit/_search` and `/_audit/_verify` on [`Privilege::AuditRead`].
245	///
246	/// Enforced in the handlers rather than in [`authz_middleware`] for the reason
247	/// the [`Principal`] extractor re-derives instead of reading an extension: a
248	/// handler that authorizes must be safe on any router it is mounted on. The
249	/// middleware also short-circuits the superuser before it classifies anything,
250	/// so a cluster-level check does not belong there.
251	pub fn authorize_audit_read(principal: &Principal) -> Result<(), Response> {
252	    if holds_audit_read(principal) {
253	        Ok(())
254	    } else {
255	        Err(forbidden(principal, "_audit", Privilege::AuditRead))
256	    }
257	}
258	
259	/// Authorize `principal` for `privilege` on brain `brain` — i.e. on its edges
260	/// index. Every `/_graph/{brain}/*` handler calls this before it does anything
261	/// else that could reveal whether the brain exists.
262	pub fn authorize_brain(
263	    principal: &Principal,
264	    brain: &str,
265	    privilege: Privilege,
266	) -> Result<(), Response> {
267	    authorize_index(principal, &brain_edges_index(brain), privilege)
268	}
269	
270	/// Authorize `principal` for `privilege` on agent-memory namespace `ns`.
271	pub fn authorize_memory_namespace(
272	    principal: &Principal,
273	    ns: &str,
274	    privilege: Privilege,
275	) -> Result<(), Response> {
276	    authorize_index(principal, &memory_namespace_index(ns), privilege)
277	}
278	
279	/// ES-shaped 403. Names the resource and the privilege the caller lacks — the
280	/// caller supplied the resource name, so echoing it back confirms nothing —
281	/// and points at the grant that would fix it.
282	pub fn forbidden(principal: &Principal, resource: &str, privilege: Privilege) -> Response {
283	    let action = match privilege {
284	        Privilege::ReadIndex => "read",
285	        Privilege::WriteIndex => "write",
286	        Privilege::AdminIndex => "manage",
287	        Privilege::SnapshotCreate => "create_snapshot",
288	        Privilege::SnapshotRestore => "restore_snapshot",
289	        Privilege::SecurityAdmin => "manage_security",
290	        Privilege::AuditRead => "read_audit",
291	    };
292	    // `read_audit` is the one privilege here that is *not* index-scoped, so the
293	    // stock "grant it on that index" remedy would send the operator to write a
294	    // grant that cannot exist. Point at the cluster grant that actually works
295	    // (issue #329).
296	    let reason = if privilege == Privilege::AuditRead {
297	        format!(
298	            "action [{action}] is unauthorized for this credential on [{resource}]: the audit log \
299	             is not index-scoped — mint a key whose role_descriptors grant cluster [\"read_audit\"] \
300	             (POST /_security/api_key), or use the configured admin key"
301	        )
302	    } else {
303	        format!(
304	            "action [{action}] is unauthorized for this credential on [{resource}]: mint a key \
305	             whose role_descriptors grant [{action}] on that index (POST /_security/api_key), or \
306	             use the configured admin key"
307	        )
308	    };
309	    tracing::debug!(
310	        principal = principal.label(),
311	        resource,
312	        action,
313	        "authorization denied"
314	    );
315	    es_error(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, reason)
316	}
317	
318	fn es_error(status: StatusCode, reason: String) -> Response {
319	    let error_type = "security_exception".to_string();
320	    let body = EsErrorResponse {
321	        error: EsErrorBody {
322	            root_cause: vec![EsRootCause {
323	                error_type: error_type.clone(),
324	                reason: reason.clone(),
325	                resource_type: None,
326	                resource_id: None,
327	                index_uuid: None,
328	                index: None,
329	            }],
330	            error_type,
331	            reason,
332	            resource_type: None,
333	            resource_id: None,
334	            index_uuid: None,
335	            index: None,
336	            request_id: None,
337	        },
338	        status: status.as_u16(),
339	        xerj_hint: None,
340	    };
341	    (status, Json(body)).into_response()
342	}
343	
344	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
345	// The request's visible set (layer 2)
346	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
347	
348	/// Adapts a [`Principal`] to the engine's [`IndexVisibility`] hook.
349	///
350	/// "Visible" is *any* index privilege, not a specific one: this layer decides
351	/// whether the principal may reach the index at all, which is the property that
352	/// closes a body-named target the middleware did not know to parse. Which
353	/// privilege the request needs on it stays the middleware's decision, so a
354	/// read-only grant still cannot write through the front door.
355	struct PrincipalVisibility(Principal);
356	
357	impl IndexVisibility for PrincipalVisibility {
358	    fn visible(&self, index: &str) -> bool {
359	        self.0.allows_index(index, Privilege::ReadIndex)
360	            || self.0.allows_index(index, Privilege::WriteIndex)
361	            || self.0.allows_index(index, Privilege::AdminIndex)
362	    }
363	}
364	
365	/// The visibility rule for `principal`, for installing around a request.
366	pub fn visibility_for(principal: &Principal) -> Arc<dyn IndexVisibility> {
367	    Arc::new(PrincipalVisibility(principal.clone()))
368	}

370	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
371	// Request classification
372	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
373	
374	/// What a request path targets.
375	///
376	/// `op_start` on [`Target::Indices`] is the segment index at which the
377	/// operation begins, because the two routers spell resources differently:
378	/// ES-compat puts the index first (`/{index}/_search`, op at 1) while the
379	/// native router nests it (`/v1/indices/{index}/search`, op at 3). Both are
380	/// doors into the reserved namespace, so both are classified here.
381	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
382	enum Target {
383	    /// `/_graph/{brain}/…`
384	    Brain(String),
385	    /// `/_memory/{namespace}[/…]`
386	    Memory(String),
387	    /// One or more index expressions, plus where the op segment starts.
388	    Indices(Vec<String>, usize),
389	    /// A cluster/global endpoint whose path names no index: `/_cat/*`,
390	    /// `/_mapping`, `/_nodes`, but also `/_search`, `/_bulk`, `/_msearch`.
391	    /// Reads are answered over the principal's visible set; mutations must
392	    /// name their targets in the body (which [`body_targets`] extracts and
393	    /// authorizes) or belong to a principal that holds the general surface.
394	    Cluster,
395	    /// Not authorization-relevant (health probes, the version banner).
396	    Exempt,
397	}

462	/// Split a URI path into percent-decoded, non-empty segments.
463	fn segments(path: &str) -> Vec<String> {
464	    path.split('/')
465	        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
466	        .map(percent_decode)
467	        .collect()
468	}
469	
470	/// Minimal percent-decoder. The middleware compares raw path text against
471	/// index names, so `%2Exerj-memory-alice-edges` must not slip past a check
472	/// that `.xerj-memory-alice-edges` would fail. Invalid escapes are left
473	/// verbatim (they cannot decode into the reserved prefix).
474	fn percent_decode(s: &str) -> String {
475	    if !s.contains('%') {
476	        return s.to_string();
477	    }
478	    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
479	    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());
480	    let mut i = 0;
481	    while i < bytes.len() {
482	        if bytes[i] == b'%' && i + 2 < bytes.len() {
483	            let hex = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[i + 1..i + 3]).ok();
484	            if let Some(b) = hex.and_then(|h| u8::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok()) {
485	                out.push(b);
486	                i += 3;
487	                continue;
488	            }
489	        }
490	        out.push(bytes[i]);
491	        i += 1;
492	    }
493	    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()
494	}

496	/// Classify a request path.
497	fn classify(path: &str) -> Target {
498	    // Probes, the scrape endpoint, and "who am I" — none of which name or
499	    // reveal an index. `_security/_authenticate` in particular must stay open
500	    // to a scoped key, or a caller cannot verify its own credential.
501	    if AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS.contains(&path)
502	        || path == "/v1/metrics"
503	        || path == "/_security/_authenticate"
504	        // `POST /_share/claim` is unauthenticated by design (the guest
505	        // has no key yet) and names no index; the handler decides everything.
506	        || crate::auth::is_share_claim_path(path)
507	    {
508	        return Target::Exempt;
509	    }
510	    let segs = segments(path);
511	    let Some(first) = segs.first() else {
512	        // `GET /` — the version banner. No data.
513	        return Target::Exempt;
514	    };
515	    match first.as_str() {
516	        "_graph" => match segs.get(1) {
517	            Some(brain) => Target::Brain(brain.clone()),
518	            // No brain in the path: no route matches, let it 404.
519	            None => Target::Exempt,
520	        },
521	        "_memory" => match segs.get(1) {
522	            Some(ns) => Target::Memory(ns.clone()),
523	            None => Target::Exempt,
524	        },
525	        // Native router (`build_native_router`, :8080). Same engine, same
526	        // indices, different spelling — and therefore the same boundary:
527	        // `GET /v1/indices/.xerj-memory-alice-edges` must be no more reachable
528	        // than `GET /.xerj-memory-alice-edges`.
529	        "v1" => match (segs.get(1).map(String::as_str), segs.get(2)) {
530	            (Some("indices"), Some(expr)) | (Some("schema"), Some(expr)) => {
531	                Target::Indices(split_expressions(expr), 3)
532	            }
533	            // `POST /v1/indices` names its index in the body — authorized as
534	            // `BodyShape::NativeCreate`, not refused for lack of a path target.
535	            _ => Target::Cluster,
536	        },
537	        // `/_all/_search` and `/*/_search` are index-scoped routes whose index
538	        // happens to be a pattern — not cluster endpoints. Classifying them
539	        // here is what lets them expand over the caller's visible set like any
540	        // other pattern instead of being refused for naming nothing.
541	        s if s == "*" || s == "_all" => Target::Indices(split_expressions(s), 1),
542	        s if s.starts_with('_') => Target::Cluster,
543	        s => Target::Indices(split_expressions(s), 1),
544	    }
545	}

547	/// Split a comma-separated multi-index expression (`logs-a,logs-b`).
548	fn split_expressions(s: &str) -> Vec<String> {
549	    s.split(',')
550	        .map(str::trim)
551	        .filter(|e| !e.is_empty())
552	        .map(String::from)
553	        .collect()
554	}

556	/// The privilege a request needs on whatever it targets.
557	///
558	/// Conservative by construction: anything not recognized as a read or a
559	/// lifecycle op is treated as a write, so an unclassified mutation can never
560	/// be waved through as a read.
561	fn required_privilege(method: &Method, segs: &[String], op_start: usize) -> Privilege {
562	    if method == Method::GET || method == Method::HEAD {
563	        return Privilege::ReadIndex;
564	    }
565	    match segs.get(op_start).map(String::as_str) {
566	        Some(o) if POST_READ_OPS.contains(&o) => Privilege::ReadIndex,
567	        Some(o) if ADMIN_OPS.contains(&o) => Privilege::AdminIndex,
568	        // No op segment at all: the request targets the index itself, so it is
569	        // creating or destroying it.
570	        None => Privilege::AdminIndex,
571	        _ => Privilege::WriteIndex,
572	    }
573	}

575	/// Does this cluster-level request only *read*?
576	///
577	/// `GET`/`HEAD` always do. So does any verb whose op is one of the read ops:
578	/// `POST /_search`, `/_count`, `/_msearch`, `/_mget` are the reason the global
579	/// verbs are usable at all, and `DELETE /_search/scroll` / `DELETE /_pit` /
580	/// `DELETE /_async_search/{id}` release a session the caller already opened.
581	fn cluster_is_read(method: &Method, segs: &[String]) -> bool {
582	    if method == Method::GET || method == Method::HEAD {
583	        return true;
584	    }
585	    match segs.first().map(String::as_str) {
586	        Some(op) => POST_READ_OPS.contains(&op),
587	        None => true,
588	    }
589	}

591	/// The privilege a `/_graph/{brain}/…` or `/_memory/{ns}[/…]` request needs.
592	///
593	/// Kept separate from [`required_privilege`] because these paths spell their
594	/// ops without a leading underscore (`link`) and because deleting a whole
595	/// namespace is a lifecycle op while deleting one document is not.
596	fn reserved_api_privilege(method: &Method, segs: &[String]) -> Privilege {
597	    if method == Method::GET || method == Method::HEAD {
598	        return Privilege::ReadIndex;
599	    }
600	    if method == Method::POST {
601	        // `POST /_memory/{ns}/_recall` reads; `POST /_memory/{ns}` and
602	        // `POST /_graph/{b}/link` write. Creating the backing index lazily is
603	        // part of writing a brain, not a separate `manage` step.
604	        return if segs.iter().any(|s| s == "_recall") {
605	            Privilege::ReadIndex
606	        } else {
607	            Privilege::WriteIndex
608	        };
609	    }
610	    if method == Method::DELETE {
611	        // `DELETE /_memory/{ns}` drops the whole namespace → manage.
612	        // `DELETE /_memory/{ns}/{id}` and `DELETE /_graph/{b}/link/{id}` are
613	        // document-level → write.
614	        return if segs.len() <= 2 {
615	            Privilege::AdminIndex
616	        } else {
617	            Privilege::WriteIndex
618	        };
619	    }
620	    Privilege::WriteIndex
621	}

627	/// The shape in which a route's body can name the indices it operates on.
628	///
629	/// This table is the exhaustive answer to "which handlers take an index from
630	/// the request body". It is not the *only* protection — [`PrincipalVisibility`]
631	/// in the engine catches whatever is missing from it — but it is what produces
632	/// a precise 403 with the right privilege instead of a downstream "not found".
633	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
634	enum BodyShape {
635	    /// Nothing in the body names an index.
636	    None,
637	    /// `_bulk` NDJSON: `{"index"|"create"|"update"|"delete": {"_index": …}}`.
638	    Bulk,
639	    /// `_msearch` / `_msearch/template` NDJSON header lines: `{"index": …}`,
640	    /// where the value may be a string or an array of strings.
641	    MsearchHeaders,
642	    /// `_mget`: `{"docs": [{"_index": …}]}`.
643	    MgetDocs,
644	    /// `POST /_aliases`: `{"actions": [{"add"|"remove"|"remove_index": …}]}`.
645	    AliasActions,
646	    /// `_reindex`: `{"source": {"index": …}, "dest": {"index": …}}`.
647	    Reindex,
648	    /// Snapshot create / restore: `{"indices": "a,b" | ["a","b"]}`.
649	    SnapshotIndices,
650	    /// Native `POST /v1/indices`: `{"name": …}`.
651	    NativeCreate,
652	    /// `PUT /{index}`: the `aliases` block creates alias names.
653	    CreateIndex,
654	    /// Any search-shaped body — a `terms` lookup names another index to read
655	    /// its terms out of, at arbitrary depth.
656	    Query,
657	    /// `POST /_monitoring/bulk` writes one fixed internal index.
658	    MonitoringBulk,
659	    /// An index template's `index_patterns`. It names no index that exists
660	    /// yet, but it decides the mapping of every index created under a matching
661	    /// name later — including a brain — so the patterns are checked in their
662	    /// own right by [`authorize_template_patterns`].
663	    IndexTemplate,
664	    /// An ML job or datafeed config: `PUT /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{id}`
665	    /// (`source_index`, `index`, and the combined-form `datafeed_config`) and
666	    /// `PUT /_ml/datafeeds/{id}` (`indices` / `indexes`).
667	    ///
668	    /// These name an index the *server* will go and read, on a schedule, on
669	    /// the caller's behalf. Registering one against an index the caller cannot
670	    /// read is wrong on its own terms — it was accepted with a 200 before this
671	    /// arm existed — and it was also the front half of a live cross-brain
672	    /// read: the detached scorer `POST /_ml/datafeeds/{id}/_start` spawns had
673	    /// no visibility rule, so it fetched what the caller could not. The
674	    /// detached half is fixed at the spawn site (`es_compat`'s
675	    /// `spawn_datafeed_task` carries the rule across); this is the half that
676	    /// refuses the configuration in the first place.
677	    MlConfig,
678	}

681	const QUERY_BODY_OPS: &[&str] = &[
682	    "_search",
683	    "_count",
684	    "_explain",
685	    "_validate",
686	    "_delete_by_query",
687	    "_update_by_query",
688	    "_async_search",
689	    "_eql",
690	    "_rank_eval",
691	    "_terms_enum",
692	    "_field_caps",
693	    "_knn_search",
694	    "_pit",
695	    "_graph",
696	    "_sql",
697	    "_esql",
698	];

700	/// The index `POST /_monitoring/bulk` ingests into
701	/// (`es_compat::ingest_monitoring_ndjson`).
702	const MONITORING_INDEX: &str = "xerj-monitoring";
703	
704	/// Which body shape does this route carry?
705	fn body_shape(method: &Method, segs: &[String]) -> BodyShape {
706	    let first = segs.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("");
707	    // Native router. Its ingest bodies are plain document arrays under an
708	    // index named in the path; the only body-named index it has is the create.
709	    if first == "v1" {
710	        return match (segs.get(1).map(String::as_str), segs.len()) {
711	            (Some("indices"), 2) if method == Method::POST => BodyShape::NativeCreate,
712	            _ => BodyShape::None,
713	        };
714	    }
715	    let has = |op: &str| segs.iter().any(|s| s == op);
716	    if has("_bulk") {
717	        return BodyShape::Bulk;
718	    }
719	    if has("_msearch") {
720	        return BodyShape::MsearchHeaders;
721	    }
722	    if has("_mget") {
723	        return BodyShape::MgetDocs;
724	    }
725	    if first == "_aliases" && method != Method::GET {
726	        return BodyShape::AliasActions;
727	    }
728	    if first == "_reindex" {
729	        return BodyShape::Reindex;
730	    }
731	    if first == "_snapshot" {
732	        return BodyShape::SnapshotIndices;
733	    }
734	    if first == "_monitoring" {
735	        return BodyShape::MonitoringBulk;
736	    }
737	    if (first == "_index_template" || first == "_template") && method != Method::GET {
738	        return BodyShape::IndexTemplate;
739	    }
740	    // `PUT|POST /_ml/anomaly_detectors/{id}` and `PUT|POST /_ml/datafeeds/{id}`
741	    // — exactly three segments, so the sub-verbs (`…/{id}/_start`, `_stop`,
742	    // `_score`, `results/records`) are not swept in: they carry no index name
743	    // of their own, and their reach is decided by the config that was already
744	    // authorized here plus the guard the spawned scorer carries.
745	    if first == "_ml" && segs.len() == 3 && (method == Method::PUT || method == Method::POST) {
746	        return match segs[1].as_str() {
747	            "anomaly_detectors" | "datafeeds" => BodyShape::MlConfig,
748	            _ => BodyShape::None,
749	        };
750	    }
751	    if segs.len() == 1 && method == Method::PUT && !first.starts_with('_') {
752	        return BodyShape::CreateIndex;
753	    }
754	    if QUERY_BODY_OPS.iter().any(|op| has(op)) {
755	        return BodyShape::Query;
756	    }
757	    BodyShape::None
758	}

760	/// One index expression a request will touch, and what it needs on it.
761	type Demand = (String, Privilege);
762	
763	/// Refuse a request whose body should have named its targets but could not be
764	/// parsed. Fail-closed: an unreadable target is not an absent one.
765	fn unresolvable(principal: &Principal, what: &str) -> Response {
766	    tracing::debug!(
767	        principal = principal.label(),
768	        what,
769	        "authorization refused: request body names indices but could not be resolved"
770	    );
771	    es_error(
772	        StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,
773	        format!(
774	            "this credential is authorized per index, and the {what} could not be resolved from \
775	             the request body; send a well-formed body that names its indices"
776	        ),
777	    )
778	}
779	
780	/// Extract every index this request's **body** will touch, with the privilege
781	/// it needs on each.
782	///
783	/// `default_index` is the path index for the index-scoped spellings
784	/// (`/{index}/_bulk`, `/{index}/_msearch`, `/{index}/_mget`), which the body
785	/// may override — the override being the whole bug this exists for.
786	fn body_targets(
787	    principal: &Principal,
788	    shape: BodyShape,
789	    body: &[u8],
790	    default_index: Option<&str>,
791	) -> Result<Vec<Demand>, Response> {
792	    let mut out: Vec<Demand> = Vec::new();
793	    match shape {
794	        BodyShape::None => {}
795	        BodyShape::MonitoringBulk => {
796	            out.push((MONITORING_INDEX.to_string(), Privilege::WriteIndex))
797	        }
798	        BodyShape::Bulk => {
799	            // NDJSON, alternating action and (except for `delete`) source
800	            // lines. Every action line must parse — one that does not is a
801	            // target we cannot see, so the request is refused rather than
802	            // handed to a bulk pipeline that would happily route it.
803	            let Ok(text) = std::str::from_utf8(body) else {
804	                return Err(unresolvable(principal, "bulk action lines"));
805	            };
806	            // Fast path for the index-scoped spelling every client uses by
807	            // default: with no `_index` anywhere in the payload, every action
808	            // targets the path index, and there is nothing to find by parsing
809	            // a million action lines.
810	            if !text.contains("\"_index\"") {
811	                if let Some(d) = default_index {
812	                    out.push((d.to_string(), Privilege::WriteIndex));
813	                }
814	                return Ok(out);
815	            }
816	            let mut expect_action = true;
817	            for line in text.lines() {
818	                let line = line.trim();
819	                if line.is_empty() {
820	                    continue;
821	                }
822	                if !expect_action {
823	                    expect_action = true;
824	                    continue;
825	                }
826	                let Ok(action) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line) else {
827	                    return Err(unresolvable(principal, "bulk action lines"));
828	                };
829	                let Some(obj) = action.as_object() else {
830	                    return Err(unresolvable(principal, "bulk action lines"));
831	                };
832	                let Some((verb, meta)) = obj.iter().next() else {
833	                    return Err(unresolvable(principal, "bulk action lines"));
834	                };
835	                // `delete` carries no source line; everything else does.
836	                expect_action = verb == "delete";
837	                let named = meta.get("_index").and_then(Value::as_str);
838	                if let Some(index) = named.or(default_index) {
839	                    out.push((index.to_string(), Privilege::WriteIndex));
840	                }
841	            }
842	        }
843	        BodyShape::MsearchHeaders => {
844	            let Ok(text) = std::str::from_utf8(body) else {
845	                return Err(unresolvable(principal, "multi-search header lines"));
846	            };
847	            let mut expect_header = true;
848	            for line in text.lines() {
849	                let line = line.trim();
850	                if line.is_empty() {
851	                    continue;
852	                }
853	                let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line) else {
854	                    return Err(unresolvable(principal, "multi-search header lines"));
855	                };
856	                if expect_header {
857	                    match parsed.get("index") {
858	                        Some(Value::String(s)) => out.push((s.clone(), Privilege::ReadIndex)),
859	                        Some(Value::Array(items)) => {
860	                            for i in items {
861	                                if let Some(s) = i.as_str() {
862	                                    out.push((s.to_string(), Privilege::ReadIndex));
863	                                }
864	                            }
865	                        }
866	                        // A header that names no index means "the path index,
867	                        // else every index" — the latter is answered over the
868	                        // visible set, so nothing to demand here.
869	                        _ => {
870	                            if let Some(d) = default_index {
871	                                out.push((d.to_string(), Privilege::ReadIndex));
872	                            }
873	                        }
874	                    }
875	                } else {
876	                    // The search body half — it can still carry a terms lookup.
877	                    collect_query_body_indices(&parsed, &mut out);
878	                }
879	                expect_header = !expect_header;
880	            }
881	        }
882	        BodyShape::MgetDocs => {
883	            let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body) else {
884	                return Err(unresolvable(principal, "multi-get documents"));
885	            };
886	            match parsed.get("docs").and_then(Value::as_array) {
887	                Some(docs) => {
888	                    for doc in docs {
889	                        let named = doc.get("_index").and_then(Value::as_str);
890	                        match named.or(default_index) {
891	                            Some(index) => out.push((index.to_string(), Privilege::ReadIndex)),
892	                            None => return Err(unresolvable(principal, "multi-get documents")),
893	                        }
894	                    }
895	                }
896	                // `{"ids": [...]}` short form uses the path index.
897	                None => {
898	                    if let Some(d) = default_index {
899	                        out.push((d.to_string(), Privilege::ReadIndex));
900	                    }
901	                }
902	            }
903	        }
904	        BodyShape::AliasActions => {
905	            let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body) else {
906	                return Err(unresolvable(principal, "alias actions"));
907	            };
908	            let Some(actions) = parsed.get("actions").and_then(Value::as_array) else {
909	                return Err(unresolvable(principal, "alias actions"));
910	            };
911	            for action in actions {
912	                let Some(obj) = action.as_object() else {
913	                    return Err(unresolvable(principal, "alias actions"));
914	                };
915	                for (_verb, params) in obj {
916	                    // Pointing an alias at an index is a change to that index's
917	                    // addressing, so it needs `manage` on it — the same
918	                    // privilege `PUT /{index}/_alias/{alias}` already demands.
919	                    push_names(params.get("index"), Privilege::AdminIndex, &mut out);
920	                    push_names(params.get("indices"), Privilege::AdminIndex, &mut out);
921	                    // …and the alias NAME is authorized in its own right, so a
922	                    // caller cannot squat an alias inside the reserved
923	                    // namespace and have a brain resolve through it later.
924	                    push_names(params.get("alias"), Privilege::AdminIndex, &mut out);
925	                    push_names(params.get("aliases"), Privilege::AdminIndex, &mut out);
926	                }
927	            }
928	            if out.is_empty() {
929	                return Err(unresolvable(principal, "alias actions"));
930	            }
931	        }
932	        BodyShape::Reindex => {
933	            let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body) else {
934	                return Err(unresolvable(principal, "reindex source and destination"));
935	            };
936	            let before = out.len();
937	            if let Some(source) = parsed.get("source") {
938	                push_names(source.get("index"), Privilege::ReadIndex, &mut out);
939	                push_names(source.get("indices"), Privilege::ReadIndex, &mut out);
940	                if let Some(q) = source.get("query") {
941	                    collect_query_body_indices(q, &mut out);
942	                }
943	            }
944	            if let Some(dest) = parsed.get("dest") {
945	                push_names(dest.get("index"), Privilege::WriteIndex, &mut out);
946	            }
947	            if out.len() == before {
948	                return Err(unresolvable(principal, "reindex source and destination"));
949	            }
950	        }
951	        BodyShape::SnapshotIndices => {
952	            // Absent `indices` means "every index on the node", which for a
953	            // non-superuser would be a bulk read (or overwrite) of every
954	            // brain. `decide` turns an empty demand list on this route into a
955	            // refusal; here we only report what was named. A restore *writes*
956	            // its targets — `decide` upgrades the privilege, since only the
957	            // path says which of the two this is.
958	            if let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body) {
959	                push_names(parsed.get("indices"), Privilege::ReadIndex, &mut out);
960	            }
961	        }
962	        BodyShape::NativeCreate => {
963	            let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body) else {
964	                return Err(unresolvable(principal, "index name"));
965	            };
966	            match parsed.get("name").and_then(Value::as_str) {
967	                Some(name) => out.push((name.to_string(), Privilege::AdminIndex)),
968	                None => return Err(unresolvable(principal, "index name")),
969	            }
970	        }
971	        BodyShape::CreateIndex => {
972	            // `PUT /{index}` names its index in the path (already demanded);
973	            // its body can additionally mint alias names.
974	            if let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body) {
975	                if let Some(aliases) = parsed.get("aliases").and_then(Value::as_object) {
976	                    for alias in aliases.keys() {
977	                        out.push((alias.clone(), Privilege::AdminIndex));
978	                    }
979	                }
980	            }
981	        }
982	        BodyShape::Query => {
983	            if let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body) {
984	                collect_query_body_indices(&parsed, &mut out);
985	            }
986	        }
987	        BodyShape::MlConfig => {
988	            let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body) else {
989	                // Not JSON: it names no index, and the handler will reject it
990	                // for the missing `source_index` / `job_id` anyway.
991	                return Ok(out);
992	            };
993	            // Every spelling the two ML handlers actually read. `put_ml_datafeed`
994	            // takes `indices` OR `indexes`; `put_ml_anomaly_detector` takes
995	            // `source_index` (string or array) OR `index`; the ES combined form
996	            // nests a whole datafeed under `datafeed_config`.
997	            let push_ml = |v: Option<&Value>, out: &mut Vec<Demand>| {
998	                push_names(v, Privilege::ReadIndex, out);
999	            };
1000	            push_ml(parsed.get("source_index"), &mut out);
1001	            push_ml(parsed.get("index"), &mut out);
1002	            push_ml(parsed.get("indices"), &mut out);
1003	            push_ml(parsed.get("indexes"), &mut out);
1004	            if let Some(dfc) = parsed.get("datafeed_config") {
1005	                push_ml(dfc.get("indices"), &mut out);
1006	                push_ml(dfc.get("indexes"), &mut out);
1007	                push_ml(dfc.get("index"), &mut out);
1008	            }
1009	            // A body that names nothing is NOT refused: `PUT /_ml/datafeeds/{id}`
1010	            // may carry only a `job_id`, in which case the handler inherits the
1011	            // detector's `source_index` — a name this middleware cannot see, but
1012	            // one that was authorized when the detector itself was created, and
1013	            // that the scorer re-checks under the starter's own visibility rule.
1014	            // `decide` reads the empty list on this shape as "nothing named",
1015	            // not as "unrestricted".
1016	        }
1017	        // Patterns, not names — `authorize_template_patterns` handles them.
1018	        BodyShape::IndexTemplate => {}
1019	    }
1020	    // A bulk usually names two or three indices across a million action lines.
1021	    out.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0).then(rank(a.1).cmp(&rank(b.1))));
1022	    out.dedup();
1023	    Ok(out)
1024	}

1026	/// Stable ordering key for a privilege, so the demand list can be deduped
1027	/// without asking `xerj_engine::rbac` for an `Ord` it has no other use for.
1028	fn rank(p: Privilege) -> u8 {
1029	    match p {
1030	        Privilege::ReadIndex => 0,
1031	        Privilege::WriteIndex => 1,
1032	        Privilege::AdminIndex => 2,
1033	        Privilege::SnapshotCreate => 3,
1034	        Privilege::SnapshotRestore => 4,
1035	        Privilege::SecurityAdmin => 5,
1036	        Privilege::AuditRead => 6,
1037	    }
1038	}

1040	/// An index template applies to indices that do not exist yet, so there is no
1041	/// name to authorize — only a pattern. A template whose `index_patterns` can
1042	/// match the reserved namespace would pick the mapping of a brain created
1043	/// later, which is a write to that brain by another route, so a non-superuser
1044	/// may not register one.
1045	fn authorize_template_patterns(principal: &Principal, body: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Response> {
1046	    let Ok(parsed) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body) else {
1047	        // Not JSON: it names no pattern, and the handler will reject it.
1048	        return Ok(());
1049	    };
1050	    let mut patterns: Vec<Demand> = Vec::new();
1051	    push_names(
1052	        parsed.get("index_patterns"),
1053	        Privilege::AdminIndex,
1054	        &mut patterns,
1055	    );
1056	    // ES 6-era `_template` spelled it `template`.
1057	    push_names(parsed.get("template"), Privilege::AdminIndex, &mut patterns);
1058	    for (pattern, _) in patterns {
1059	        if !may_reach_reserved(&pattern) {
1060	            continue;
1061	        }
1062	        // Only a principal that was *granted* the namespace may template over
1063	        // it. `Unscoped::allows_index` answers "not reserved" for a pattern
1064	        // like `*` — true of the literal text, useless as an answer here — so
1065	        // it is excluded explicitly rather than consulted.
1066	        let held = match principal {
1067	            Principal::Superuser => true,
1068	            Principal::Scoped { .. } => principal.allows_index(&pattern, Privilege::AdminIndex),
1069	            _ => false,
1070	        };
1071	        if !held {
1072	            return Err(forbidden(principal, &pattern, Privilege::AdminIndex));
1073	        }
1074	    }
1075	    Ok(())
1076	}

1078	/// Push a `"a"` / `"a,b"` / `["a","b"]` index field onto the demand list.
1079	fn push_names(v: Option<&Value>, privilege: Privilege, out: &mut Vec<Demand>) {
1080	    match v {
1081	        Some(Value::String(s)) => {
1082	            for part in split_expressions(s) {
1083	                out.push((part, privilege));
1084	            }
1085	        }
1086	        Some(Value::Array(items)) => {
1087	            for item in items {
1088	                if let Some(s) = item.as_str() {
1089	                    for part in split_expressions(s) {
1090	                        out.push((part, privilege));
1091	                    }
1092	                }
1093	            }
1094	        }
1095	        _ => {}
1096	    }
1097	}

1099	/// Collect every index a **search body** reads that the URL never names.
1100	///
1101	/// Two shapes, both found by auditing the tree rather than by being attacked —
1102	/// which is the point of auditing:
1103	///
1104	/// - a `terms` lookup, `{"terms": {"field": {"index": "other", "id": "1",
1105	///   "path": "vals"}}}`, fetches a document out of `other` and substitutes its
1106	///   values into the query;
1107	/// - a `lookup` runtime field, `{"runtime_mappings": {"f": {"type": "lookup",
1108	///   "target_index": "other", …}}}`, joins rows out of `other` into the hits.
1109	///
1110	/// Both are matched structurally (the full lookup triple, the `type: lookup`
1111	/// marker) rather than on the key name alone, so a document field that happens
1112	/// to be called `index` is never mistaken for one.
1113	fn collect_query_body_indices(q: &Value, out: &mut Vec<Demand>) {
1114	    match q {
1115	        Value::Object(obj) => {
1116	            if let Some(Value::Object(terms)) = obj.get("terms") {
1117	                for (field, spec) in terms {
1118	                    if field == "boost" {
1119	                        continue;
1120	                    }
1121	                    if let Some(s) = spec.as_object() {
1122	                        // Only a full lookup triple actually fetches.
1123	                        if s.contains_key("id") && s.contains_key("path") {
1124	                            if let Some(ix) = s.get("index").and_then(Value::as_str) {
1125	                                out.push((ix.to_string(), Privilege::ReadIndex));
1126	                            }
1127	                        }
1128	                    }
1129	                }
1130	            }
1131	            if obj.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("lookup") {
1132	                if let Some(ix) = obj.get("target_index").and_then(Value::as_str) {
1133	                    out.push((ix.to_string(), Privilege::ReadIndex));
1134	                }
1135	            }
1136	            for child in obj.values() {
1137	                collect_query_body_indices(child, out);
1138	            }
1139	        }
1140	        Value::Array(items) => {
1141	            for item in items {
1142	                collect_query_body_indices(item, out);
1143	            }
1144	        }
1145	        _ => {}
1146	    }
1147	}
