1180	/// Does the engine expand this request's index expressions over the
1181	/// principal's visible set, or does it act on the pattern itself?
1182	///
1183	/// The distinction decides whether a wildcard may be waved through here. It is
1184	/// [`PatternExpansion::Guarded`] almost everywhere, because a name only becomes
1185	/// an index inside [`xerj_engine::index_guard`]'s funnel.
1186	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1187	enum PatternExpansion {
1188	    /// The name is resolved through `Engine::get_index` / `list_indices` /
1189	    /// `index_name_list`, so a wildcard is expanded over what this principal
1190	    /// may see and needs no decision of its own.
1191	    Guarded,
1192	    /// The handler acts on the expression itself, outside that funnel — a
1193	    /// wildcard authorized here is a wildcard executed.
1194	    Unguarded,
1195	}
1196	
1197	/// How the route carrying `shape` resolves the names its body holds.
1198	///
1199	/// Only snapshot and restore are unguarded. `Engine::create_snapshot` walks
1200	/// the index map itself and `Engine::restore_snapshot` expands the pattern
1201	/// against the snapshot's own manifest, then `remove_dir_all`s and rewrites
1202	/// the index directory — neither goes through `get_index` or `delete_index`,
1203	/// which is where every other body-named target meets the visibility guard.
1204	fn expansion_for(shape: BodyShape) -> PatternExpansion {
1205	    match shape {
1206	        BodyShape::SnapshotIndices => PatternExpansion::Unguarded,
1207	        _ => PatternExpansion::Guarded,
1208	    }
1209	}

1211	/// Authorize one index expression, resolving aliases first.
1212	///
1213	/// Under [`PatternExpansion::Guarded`] a pattern is *not* refused: it is
1214	/// expanded over the principal's visible set by the engine (see
1215	/// [`xerj_engine::index_guard`]), so a granted `logs-*` works and an ungranted
1216	/// `*` silently resolves to nothing instead of leaking what it would have
1217	/// matched.
1218	///
1219	/// Under [`PatternExpansion::Unguarded`] that reasoning does not hold, so a
1220	/// pattern that [`may_reach_reserved`] is decided here, on the same terms as an
1221	/// index template's `index_patterns`: only a principal explicitly *granted* the
1222	/// pattern may use it. Anything narrower (`logs-*`) still passes — it cannot
1223	/// name a brain, and refusing it would cost the ordinary per-tenant backup.
1224	fn authorize_expression(
1225	    principal: &Principal,
1226	    aliases: &dyn AliasResolver,
1227	    expr: &str,
1228	    privilege: Privilege,
1229	    expansion: PatternExpansion,
1230	) -> Result<(), Response> {
1231	    if is_pattern(expr) {
1232	        if expansion == PatternExpansion::Guarded || !may_reach_reserved(expr) {
1233	            return Ok(());
1234	        }
1235	        // `Unscoped::allows_index` answers "not reserved" for the literal text
1236	        // `*` — true of the string, useless as an answer here — so it is
1237	        // excluded explicitly rather than consulted, exactly as in
1238	        // `authorize_template_patterns`.
1239	        let held = match principal {
1240	            Principal::Superuser => true,
1241	            Principal::Scoped { .. } => principal.allows_index(expr, privilege),
1242	            _ => false,
1243	        };
1244	        return if held {
1245	            Ok(())
1246	        } else {
1247	            Err(forbidden(principal, expr, privilege))
1248	        };
1249	    }
1250	    match aliases.targets(expr) {
1251	        Some(backing) if !backing.is_empty() => {
1252	            for index in backing {
1253	                authorize_index(principal, &index, privilege)?;
1254	            }
1255	            Ok(())
1256	        }
1257	        _ => authorize_index(principal, expr, privilege),
1258	    }
1259	}

1265	/// Largest response this middleware will buffer in order to prune reserved
1266	/// index names out of it. Metadata listings are kilobytes; the cap only exists
1267	/// so a pathological response cannot be turned into an OOM.
1268	const MAX_PRUNABLE_RESPONSE_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;

1270	/// Set on every response this middleware produced itself — a refusal, so the
1271	/// handler never ran.
1272	///
1273	/// [`crate::audit_mw`] needs the distinction. The `_share` and
1274	/// `_security/api_key` handlers write their own audit entries, so the
1275	/// request-level layer used to skip those paths entirely — and a request that
1276	/// was stopped *here* reached neither: a share-link guest's `POST /_share`,
1277	/// `DELETE /_share/{handle}` and `POST /_security/api_key` all answered `403`
1278	/// and left no trace (review of PR #947, reproduced 2026-09-19: four refused
1279	/// calls, zero audit lines). Those are the escalation probes an owner most
1280	/// wants recorded. The marker lets the audit layer record exactly the requests
1281	/// the handler could not, without doubling the ones it could.
1282	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
1283	pub struct RefusedBeforeHandler;

1285	fn refused(mut resp: Response) -> Response {
1286	    resp.extensions_mut().insert(RefusedBeforeHandler);

1290	/// Authorization middleware for both routers.
1291	///
1292	/// Layered *inside* [`crate::auth::auth_middleware`] (added to the router
1293	/// before it, so it runs after it): authentication has already rejected
1294	/// anonymous callers, and this decides what the authenticated one may reach.
1295	///
1296	/// A superuser — open mode (`--insecure`, point-at-a-folder) or the configured
1297	/// admin key — short-circuits on the first line, so the zero-configuration
1298	/// local path pays nothing: no body buffering, no visibility guard, no
1299	/// response pruning.
1300	pub async fn authz_middleware(State(state): State<AppState>, req: Request, next: Next) -> Response {
1301	    let path = req.uri().path().to_string();
1302	    let target = classify(&path);
1303	    if matches!(target, Target::Exempt) {
1304	        // `/v1/metrics` is exempt because it names no index — but it does
1305	        // describe the node (index counts, document counts, request rates),
1306	        // which is more than a share-link guest was handed. Every other exempt
1307	        // path is a probe, the version banner, "who am I" or the claim route
1308	        // itself. Authenticating here costs one header lookup on the scrape
1309	        // path only.
1310	        if path == "/v1/metrics" {
1311	            let principal = authenticate(
1312	                &state,
1313	                req.headers()
1314	                    .get(header::AUTHORIZATION)
1315	                    .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()),
1316	            );
1317	            if principal.is_share_guest() {
1318	                return refused(guest_forbidden(&principal, &path));
1319	            }
1320	        }
1321	        return next.run(req).await;
1322	    }
1323	
1324	    let principal = authenticate(
1325	        &state,
1326	        req.headers()
1327	            .get(header::AUTHORIZATION)
1328	            .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()),
1329	    );
1330	    if principal.is_superuser() {
1331	        return next.run(req).await;
1332	    }
1333	
1334	    let segs = segments(&path);
1335	    let method = req.method().clone();
1336	
1337	    // A share-link guest gets a route allow-list on top of its index grants.
1338	    // Checked first and separately so that everything below still runs for a
1339	    // guest: this can only refuse, never permit.
1340	    if principal.is_share_guest()
1341	        && !guest_route_allowed(&method, &segs, &target, req.uri().query())
1342	    {
1343	        return refused(guest_forbidden(&principal, &path));
1344	    }
1345	    let shape = body_shape(&method, &segs);
1346	
1347	    // Buffer the body only for the routes that can name an index inside it.
1348	    // `Bytes` is refcounted, so handing the same buffer to the handler costs a
1349	    // clone of a pointer, not of the payload.
1350	    let (req, body) = if shape == BodyShape::None {
1351	        (req, Bytes::new())
1352	    } else {
1353	        let limit = state.config.limits.max_body_bytes;
1354	        let (parts, raw) = req.into_parts();
1355	        match axum::body::to_bytes(raw, limit).await {
1356	            Ok(bytes) => (Request::from_parts(parts, Body::from(bytes.clone())), bytes),
1357	            Err(_) => {
1358	                return es_error(
1359	                    StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE,
1360	                    "request body exceeds limits.max_body_bytes and cannot be authorized"
1361	                        .to_string(),
1362	                )
1363	            }
1364	        }
1365	    };
1366	
1367	    if principal.is_share_guest() && guest_body_denied(shape, &body) {
1368	        return refused(guest_forbidden(&principal, &path));
1369	    }
1370	
1371	    if let Err(denied) = decide(&principal, &method, &segs, &target, shape, &body, &state) {
1372	        let denied = refused(denied);
1373	        return if principal.is_share_guest() {
1374	            crate::share::no_store(denied)
1375	        } else {
1376	            denied
1377	        };
1378	    }
1379	
1380	    // Layer 2: whatever the handler resolves from here on — including names
1381	    // this module never parsed — is checked against the same principal at the
1382	    // engine's index funnel.
1383	    let response =
1384	        xerj_engine::index_guard::scoped(visibility_for(&principal), next.run(req)).await;
1385	    let response = prune_response(response, &segs, &principal, &state).await;
1386	    // What a guest reads is somebody's documents, and the road to the guest
1387	    // may run through a tunnel or a proxy the owner does not operate. Nothing
1388	    // on that road may keep a copy.
1389	    if principal.is_share_guest() {
1390	        crate::share::no_store(response)
1391	    } else {
1392	        response
1393	    }
1394	}

1420	/// (review of PR #947). An allow-list entry for a route that does not exist
1421	/// is a permission nobody tested; whoever adds the route decides then.

1429	/// May a share-link guest call this route at all?
1430	///
1431	/// A route allow-list, deliberately separate from — and applied before — the
1432	/// index decision in [`decide`]. A scoped key is normally given a *filtered*
1433	/// view of the cluster surface (`_cat`, `_cluster/*`, `_nodes`, `_snapshot`
1434	/// listings, the global `_search`), because Kibana cannot function without
1435	/// one. A guest is not Kibana: it was handed one corpus by someone who did not
1436	/// agree to describe their node. So for a guest the cluster surface is simply
1437	/// closed, and the index surface is closed except for reading.
1438	///
1439	/// Returning `true` permits nothing on its own; [`decide`] still checks every
1440	/// named index against the key's grants.
1441	fn guest_route_allowed(
1442	    method: &Method,
1443	    segs: &[String],
1444	    target: &Target,
1445	    query: Option<&str>,
1446	) -> bool {
1447	    let is_get = method == Method::GET || method == Method::HEAD;
1448	    let is_read_verb = is_get || method == Method::POST;
1449	    match target {
1450	        Target::Exempt => true,
1451	        Target::Cluster | Target::Memory(_) => false,
1452	        Target::Brain(_) => {
1453	            is_get
1454	                && segs.len() == 3
1455	                && segs
1456	                    .get(2)
1457	                    .is_some_and(|op| GUEST_GRAPH_OPS.contains(&op.as_str()))
1458	        }
1459	        Target::Indices(_, op_start) => {
1460	            // The native router spells the same index `/v1/indices/{name}/…`;
1461	            // the guest page speaks ES-compat only, so that door stays shut.
1462	            if segs.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("v1") {
1463	                return false;
1464	            }
1465	            let Some(op) = segs.get(*op_start).map(String::as_str) else {
1466	                // `GET /{index}` — settings, aliases and mappings in one.
1467	                return false;
1468	            };
1469	            let extra = segs.len() - op_start - 1;
1470	            let shape_ok = if GUEST_INDEX_OPS.contains(&op) {
1471	                is_read_verb && extra == 0
1472	            } else if GUEST_DOC_OPS.contains(&op) {
1473	                is_get && extra == 1
1474	            } else {
1475	                false
1476	            };
1477	            shape_ok && !query_names_any(query, GUEST_DENIED_PARAMS)
1478	        }
1479	    }
1480	}

1482	/// Does a guest's request body ask for something the route allow-list exists
1483	/// to keep shut?
1484	///
1485	/// One thing today: a point-in-time id. A guest cannot open a PIT (`_pit` is
1486	/// not on the allow-list), so any id it presents was opened by someone else —
1487	/// and a PIT, not the path, decides which index a search runs against:
1488	/// `POST /casefile/_search {"pit": {"id": <a PIT on private-diary>}}` searches
1489	/// `private-diary`. The engine's index funnel already refuses that for a
1490	/// guest (live-verified 2026-09-18: `404 no such index [private-diary]`), but
1491	/// that answer echoes the other index's name back, and the path-level decision
1492	/// above it authorized `casefile` for a request that was never going to read
1493	/// `casefile`. Refused here, by shape, for both spellings that carry a search
1494	/// body: `_search`-like bodies and `_msearch` body lines.
1495	fn guest_body_denied(shape: BodyShape, body: &[u8]) -> bool {
1496	    let has_pit = |v: &Value| v.as_object().is_some_and(|o| o.contains_key("pit"));
1497	    match shape {
1498	        BodyShape::Query => serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(body)
1499	            .map(|v| has_pit(&v))
1500	            .unwrap_or(false),
1501	        BodyShape::MsearchHeaders => body
1502	            .split(|b| *b == b'\n')
1503	            .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(line).ok())
1504	            .any(|v| has_pit(&v)),
1505	        _ => false,
1506	    }
1507	}

1509	/// Does the raw query string carry any of `names` as a parameter name?
1510	/// Names are percent-decoded and compared case-insensitively, so `%73croll`
1511	/// and `SCROLL` are the parameter they decode to.
1512	fn query_names_any(query: Option<&str>, names: &[&str]) -> bool {
1513	    let Some(query) = query else {
1514	        return false;
1515	    };
1516	    query.split('&').any(|pair| {
1517	        let key = pair.split('=').next().unwrap_or("");
1518	        let key = percent_decode(&key.replace('+', " ")).to_ascii_lowercase();
1519	        names.contains(&key.trim())
1520	    })
1521	}

1540	/// The whole decision, split out so it can be unit-tested without a router.
1541	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
1542	fn decide(
1543	    principal: &Principal,
1544	    method: &Method,
1545	    segs: &[String],
1546	    target: &Target,
1547	    shape: BodyShape,
1548	    body: &[u8],
1549	    aliases: &dyn AliasResolver,
1550	) -> Result<(), Response> {
1551	    // Restated here and not only in the middleware, so this function is a
1552	    // complete decision on its own and cannot deny the local-dev superuser if
1553	    // it is ever called from somewhere else.
1554	    if principal.is_superuser() {
1555	        return Ok(());
1556	    }
1557	    if matches!(principal, Principal::Denied) {
1558	        return Err(forbidden(principal, "<cluster>", Privilege::ReadIndex));
1559	    }
1560	    match target {
1561	        Target::Exempt => Ok(()),
1562	        Target::Brain(brain) => {
1563	            authorize_brain(principal, brain, reserved_api_privilege(method, segs))
1564	        }
1565	        Target::Memory(ns) => {
1566	            authorize_memory_namespace(principal, ns, reserved_api_privilege(method, segs))
1567	        }
1568	        Target::Indices(expressions, op_start) => {
1569	            let privilege = required_privilege(method, segs, *op_start);
1570	            for expr in expressions {
1571	                authorize_expression(
1572	                    principal,
1573	                    aliases,
1574	                    expr,
1575	                    privilege,
1576	                    PatternExpansion::Guarded,
1577	                )?;
1578	            }
1579	            // `PUT|DELETE /{index}/_alias/{alias}` mints or drops an alias
1580	            // name; the name itself is a resource, or the reserved namespace
1581	            // could be squatted by an alias nobody authorized.
1582	            if segs.get(*op_start).map(String::as_str) == Some("_alias") {
1583	                if let Some(alias) = segs.get(op_start + 1) {
1584	                    authorize_index(principal, alias, Privilege::AdminIndex)?;
1585	                }
1586	            }
1587	            // The path index is the default for a body that may override it —
1588	            // `/{index}/_bulk`, `/{index}/_msearch`, `/{index}/_mget`.
1589	            let default = expressions.first().map(String::as_str);
1590	            authorize_body(principal, aliases, shape, body, default)
1591	        }
1592	        Target::Cluster => {
1593	            // `/_xerj/*` is the node's own operator namespace, and its first
1594	            // inhabitant (`_xerj/wal_tap`, issue #320) is a whole-node export
1595	            // primitive: one `PUT` with `target_url` pointing anywhere and
1596	            // `indices: ["*"]` streams every index on this node to an
1597	            // attacker-chosen host, with an operator-supplied `Authorization`
1598	            // header attached — a data exfiltration channel and an
1599	            // authenticated SSRF in the same request.
1600	            //
1601	            // Nothing here is index-scoped, so there is no per-index decision
1602	            // to make and the reasoning is the snapshot/restore one below:
1603	            // superuser-only. That covers the reads too. `GET /_xerj/wal_tap`
1604	            // echoes `target_url` and `GET /_xerj/wal_tap/_stats` enumerates
1605	            // the node's full index inventory, and both are `cluster_is_read`,
1606	            // so without this arm a key scoped to one index could read them.
1607	            if segs.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("_xerj") {
1608	                return Err(forbidden(
1609	                    principal,
1610	                    "<node>",
1611	                    required_privilege(method, segs, 1),
1612	                ));
1613	            }
1614	            // Snapshot and restore that name no indices cover *every* index on
1615	            // the node, brains included. There is no per-index decision to
1616	            // make, so they are superuser-only.
1617	            let snapshotting = segs.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("_snapshot")
1618	                && segs.len() >= 3
1619	                && method != Method::GET
1620	                && method != Method::HEAD;
1621	            let restoring = segs.last().map(String::as_str) == Some("_restore");
1622	            if shape == BodyShape::IndexTemplate {
1623	                authorize_template_patterns(principal, body)?;
1624	            }
1625	            let mut demands = body_targets(principal, shape, body, None)?;
1626	            if restoring {
1627	                // A restore overwrites the indices it names.
1628	                for demand in demands.iter_mut() {
1629	                    demand.1 = Privilege::WriteIndex;
1630	                }
1631	            }
1632	            if snapshotting && demands.is_empty() {
1633	                return Err(forbidden(
1634	                    principal,
1635	                    "<all indices>",
1636	                    if restoring {
1637	                        Privilege::SnapshotRestore
1638	                    } else {
1639	                        Privilege::SnapshotCreate
1640	                    },
1641	                ));
1642	            }
1643	            for (expr, privilege) in &demands {
1644	                authorize_expression(principal, aliases, expr, *privilege, expansion_for(shape))?;
1645	            }
1646	            if cluster_is_read(method, segs) {
1647	                // Cluster reads (`_cat`, `_mapping`, `_nodes`, `_cluster/*`,
1648	                // and the global `_search`/`_count`/`_msearch`/`_mget`) are
1649	                // answered over the principal's visible set, so a scoped key
1650	                // gets a filtered cluster rather than a blanket 403 — which is
1651	                // what Kibana needs to function at all.
1652	                return Ok(());
1653	            }
1654	            if !demands.is_empty() {
1655	                // A mutating cluster verb that named its targets: they are all
1656	                // authorized above. `POST /_bulk`, `/_reindex` and `/_aliases`
1657	                // live here — the global bulk is the default write path for
1658	                // essentially every ES client.
1659	                return Ok(());
1660	            }
1661	            if shape == BodyShape::MlConfig {
1662	                // An ML config that named no index inherits one that was
1663	                // authorized when the detector was created (see the `MlConfig`
1664	                // arm of `body_targets`). Falling through to the
1665	                // names-nothing branch below would 403 a scoped key for the
1666	                // ordinary `PUT /_ml/datafeeds/{id} {"job_id": …}`, which
1667	                // reaches nothing this principal was not already granted.
1668	                return Ok(());
1669	            }
1670	            match principal {
1671	                // A cluster-level mutation that names nothing: an unscoped key
1672	                // keeps its historical reach over the general surface, a scoped
1673	                // one has to name what it is changing.
1674	                Principal::Unscoped { .. } => Ok(()),
1675	                _ => Err(forbidden(
1676	                    principal,
1677	                    "<cluster>",
1678	                    required_privilege(method, segs, 1),
1679	                )),
1680	            }
1681	        }
1682	    }
1683	}

1685	/// Authorize the indices a request's body names, if any.
1686	fn authorize_body(
1687	    principal: &Principal,
1688	    aliases: &dyn AliasResolver,
1689	    shape: BodyShape,
1690	    body: &[u8],
1691	    default_index: Option<&str>,
1692	) -> Result<(), Response> {
1693	    for (expr, privilege) in body_targets(principal, shape, body, default_index)? {
1694	        authorize_expression(principal, aliases, &expr, privilege, expansion_for(shape))?;
1695	    }
1696	    Ok(())
1697	}

1699	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1700	// Enumeration pruning
1701	//
1702	// Which endpoints get pruned is decided by `prune_sites` / `cat_index_columns`
1703	// below rather than by a list of path roots: an endpoint is prunable exactly
1704	// when a position is known for it, so "we prune here" and "here is where the
1705	// names are" cannot drift apart. Everything else — every search response
1706	// included — is passed through without being buffered.
1707	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1708	
1709	/// Remove index names the principal cannot read from a metadata response.
1710	///
1711	/// `Engine::list_indices` already filters, so most listings arrive clean; this
1712	/// is the second pass for the handful of handlers that read the
1713	/// `index_settings` / `index_mappings` side maps directly, and it is what keeps
1714	/// `GET /_mapping` from handing over the list of brains on the node.
1715	async fn prune_response(
1716	    response: Response,
1717	    segs: &[String],
1718	    principal: &Principal,
1719	    state: &AppState,
1720	) -> Response {
1721	    let sites = prune_sites(segs);
1722	    let columns = cat_index_columns(segs).unwrap_or(&[]);
1723	    if sites.is_empty() && columns.is_empty() {
1724	        // Nothing in this response names an index. Skip the buffer entirely —
1725	        // it is also the only correct thing to do: pruning a body with no
1726	        // index-name position in it can subtract, never protect.
1727	        return response;
1728	    }
1729	    let (parts, body) = response.into_parts();
1730	    let content_type = parts
1731	        .headers
1732	        .get(header::CONTENT_TYPE)
1733	        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
1734	        .unwrap_or("")
1735	        .to_string();
1736	    let is_json = content_type.contains("json");
1737	    let is_text = content_type.starts_with("text/");
1738	    if !is_json && !is_text {
1739	        return Response::from_parts(parts, body);
1740	    }
1741	    let bytes = match axum::body::to_bytes(body, MAX_PRUNABLE_RESPONSE_BYTES).await {
1742	        Ok(b) => b,
1743	        // Could not buffer it, so could not prune it. Refuse rather than ship
1744	        // an unfiltered listing.
1745	        Err(_) => {
1746	            return es_error(
1747	                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
1748	                "response too large to authorize; name an explicit index".to_string(),
1749	            )
1750	        }
1751	    };
1752	
1753	    // The real index names on the node. A response key is only a candidate for
1754	    // pruning when it IS one — otherwise `"mappings"`, `"settings"` and every
1755	    // other structural key would be dropped for a scoped principal, which
1756	    // would corrupt the very responses this is protecting. Read outside the
1757	    // request's visibility scope on purpose: this needs the unfiltered truth.
1758	    // Failed indices count as real names here (issue #206). They are now
1759	    // listed by `_cat/indices`, `_cat/shards` and `_cluster/state`, and a
1760	    // name that is not in this set is never a pruning candidate — so leaving
1761	    // them out would hand a scoped principal the name of a brain that
1762	    // happened to fail to open. The engine-side guard already filters them at
1763	    // the handler; this is the same second pass the open indices get.
1764	    let known: HashSet<String> = state
1765	        .engine
1766	        .index_name_list()
1767	        .into_iter()
1768	        .chain(state.engine.failed_indices.iter().map(|e| e.key().clone()))
1769	        .collect();
1770	
1771	    let pruned: Vec<u8> = if is_json {
1772	        match serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&bytes) {
1773	            Ok(mut v) => {
1774	                prune_json(&mut v, sites, principal, &known);
1775	                match serde_json::to_vec(&v) {
1776	                    Ok(v) => v,
1777	                    // Issue #204: this was
1778	                    // `.unwrap_or_else(|_| bytes.to_vec())` — a failure to
1779	                    // re-serialise the PRUNED document fell back to the
1780	                    // ORIGINAL bytes, i.e. the scoped principal received the
1781	                    // unfiltered listing this function exists to withhold.
1782	                    // Refuse, exactly as the buffering failure above does: a
1783	                    // filter that cannot run must not fail open.
1784	                    Err(e) => {
1785	                        tracing::error!(error = %e, "could not re-serialise pruned response");
1786	                        return es_error(
1787	                            StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
1788	                            "response could not be authorized".to_string(),
1789	                        );
1790	                    }
1791	                }
1792	            }
1793	            // Not JSON after all (some `_cat` handlers answer text under a
1794	            // JSON content type); fall through to the line filter.
1795	            Err(_) => prune_text(&bytes, columns, principal, &known),
1796	        }
1797	    } else {
1798	        prune_text(&bytes, columns, principal, &known)
1799	    };
1800	
1801	    let mut parts = parts;
1802	    parts.headers.remove(header::CONTENT_LENGTH);
1803	    Response::from_parts(parts, Body::from(pruned))
1804	}

1806	/// Is this index name one the principal must not even see?
1807	fn hidden(name: &str, principal: &Principal, known: &HashSet<String>) -> bool {
1808	    (is_reserved_index(name) || known.contains(name))
1809	        && !principal.allows_index(name, Privilege::ReadIndex)
1810	}

1812	/// One place in an endpoint's response where index **names** appear.
1813	///
1814	/// This exists because the first cut pruned by *key name at every depth*: any
1815	/// key equal to a real index name was deleted, wherever it appeared. An index
1816	/// name is an arbitrary string, so ordinary names collide with the structural
1817	/// keys of the very responses being pruned, and the collision only bites a
1818	/// scoped key — i.e. exactly the multi-tenant and Kibana case this whole
1819	/// branch exists to enable. Measured, on a node with one ordinary index of
1820	/// each name: `status` cost `GET /_cluster/health` its `status` field, the
1821	/// single most-polled field in the API; `indices` cost `GET /_cluster/stats`
1822	/// its entire `indices` section; `type` cost global `GET /_mapping` the `type`
1823	/// of every field definition, which is the endpoint Kibana reads to build
1824	/// index patterns.
1825	///
1826	/// So the positions are enumerated per endpoint instead, from the handlers'
1827	/// actual response shapes. `path` walks object keys from the document root,
1828	/// `/`-separated, where `*` matches any one key or array element and `""` is
1829	/// the root itself.
1830	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1831	enum Site {
1832	    /// The object at `path` is **keyed** by index name.
1833	    KeyedByIndex(&'static str),
1834	    /// The array at `path` **holds** index names: bare strings, or objects
1835	    /// whose `field` names one (`""` = bare strings only).
1836	    NamedIn(&'static str, &'static str),
1837	}
1838	
1839	/// Where index names appear in this endpoint's JSON response.
1840	///
1841	/// Anything not listed prunes nothing, which is the right default: a response
1842	/// that never names an index cannot leak one, and pruning it can only damage
1843	/// it. `_cluster/stats` is the worked example — its `indices` object holds
1844	/// aggregate counts, not a map keyed by index — and so are `_cluster/settings`,
1845	/// `_cluster/pending_tasks`, `_nodes` and `/v1/cluster/health`.
1846	fn prune_sites(segs: &[String]) -> &'static [Site] {
1847	    // `_mapping`, `_settings`, `_alias`, `_aliases`, `_recovery` and
1848	    // `_shard_stores` all answer one object keyed by index name at the root.
1849	    const ROOT_KEYED: &[Site] = &[Site::KeyedByIndex("")];
1850	    // `_stats` and `_segments` put the same map one level down.
1851	    const INDICES_KEYED: &[Site] = &[Site::KeyedByIndex("indices")];
1852	    match segs.first().map(String::as_str) {
1853	        Some("_mapping")
1854	        | Some("_mappings")
1855	        | Some("_settings")
1856	        | Some("_alias")
1857	        | Some("_aliases")
1858	        | Some("_recovery")
1859	        | Some("_shard_stores") => ROOT_KEYED,
1860	        Some("_stats") | Some("_segments") => INDICES_KEYED,
1861	        Some("_cluster") => match segs.get(1).map(String::as_str) {
1862	            // `level=indices` / `level=shards` add the per-index breakdown;
1863	            // the root is cluster-wide scalars (`status`, `timed_out`, …).
1864	            Some("health") => INDICES_KEYED,
1865	            Some("state") => &[
1866	                Site::KeyedByIndex("metadata/indices"),
1867	                Site::KeyedByIndex("routing_table/indices"),
1868	            ],
1869	            _ => &[],
1870	        },
1871	        // `{"indices": [name], "fields": {f: {type: {…, "indices": [name]}}}}`
1872	        Some("_field_caps") => &[
1873	            Site::NamedIn("indices", ""),
1874	            Site::NamedIn("fields/*/*/indices", ""),
1875	        ],
1876	        // `{"indices": [{name}], "aliases": [{name, indices}], "data_streams": []}`
1877	        Some("_resolve") => &[
1878	            Site::NamedIn("indices", "name"),
1879	            Site::NamedIn("aliases", "name"),
1880	            Site::NamedIn("aliases/*/indices", ""),
1881	            Site::NamedIn("data_streams", "name"),
1882	            Site::NamedIn("data_streams/*/backing_indices", ""),
1883	        ],
1884	        // `{"data_streams": [{name, indices: [{index_name}]}]}`
1885	        Some("_data_stream") => &[
1886	            Site::NamedIn("data_streams", "name"),
1887	            Site::NamedIn("data_streams/*/indices", "index_name"),
1888	        ],
1889	        // A `_cat` table in its `format=json` form is an array of row objects.
1890	        // Only the per-index tables have an `index` column — `_cat/templates`
1891	        // keys its rows by TEMPLATE name, which is not an index name and must
1892	        // not be matched against one.
1893	        Some("_cat") if cat_index_columns(segs).is_some() => &[Site::NamedIn("", "index")],
1894	        Some("v1") => match segs.get(1).map(String::as_str) {
1895	            // `{"data": {"indices": [{name, …}], …}}`
1896	            Some("dashboard") => &[Site::NamedIn("data/indices", "name")],
1897	            _ => &[],
1898	        },
1899	        _ => &[],
1900	    }
1901	}
1902	
1903	/// The whitespace-separated column(s) holding an index name in a `_cat`
1904	/// table's plain-text form, by sub-verb; `None` means this table has no index
1905	/// column, so no row of it may be dropped for containing an index name.
1906	///
1907	/// Column numbers are read off the handlers in `es_compat`, not guessed. The
1908	/// alternative — "drop a row if ANY token is a hidden index name" — has the
1909	/// same collision as key-matching did: an ordinary index named `open`, `green`
1910	/// or `p` that a scoped key cannot read would empty `_cat/indices` and
1911	/// `_cat/shards` completely.
1912	fn cat_index_columns(segs: &[String]) -> Option<&'static [usize]> {
1913	    match segs.get(1).map(String::as_str)? {
1914	        // health status INDEX uuid pri rep docs.count docs.deleted store …
1915	        "indices" => Some(&[2]),
1916	        // ALIAS INDEX filter routing.index routing.search is_write_index.
1917	        // Column 0 is an alias, not an index — but an alias name IS a name in
1918	        // this namespace elsewhere in this module (it is authorized as a
1919	        // resource, and it resolves to indices), so a reserved-namespace alias
1920	        // is hidden here too.
1921	        "aliases" => Some(&[0, 1]),
1922	        // INDEX shard prirep state docs store ip node
1923	        "shards" => Some(&[0]),
1924	        // INDEX shard time type stage …
1925	        "recovery" => Some(&[0]),
1926	        // INDEX shard prirep ip segment …
1927	        "segments" => Some(&[0]),
1928	        // INDEX present field nodes tombstones …
1929	        "ann" => Some(&[0]),
1930	        // id host ip node INDEX size
1931	        "fielddata" => Some(&[4]),
1932	        // Everything else under `_cat` — nodes, health, master, plugins,

1939	/// Apply `f` to every node the site `path` selects. `*` matches any one object
1940	/// key or array element; an empty path selects the node itself.
1941	fn for_each_at(v: &mut Value, path: &str, f: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Value)) {
1942	    if path.is_empty() {
1943	        f(v);
1944	        return;
1945	    }
1946	    let (head, rest) = path.split_once('/').unwrap_or((path, ""));
1947	    match v {
1948	        Value::Object(map) => {
1949	            if head == "*" {
1950	                for (_, child) in map.iter_mut() {
1951	                    for_each_at(child, rest, f);
1952	                }
1953	            } else if let Some(child) = map.get_mut(head) {
1954	                for_each_at(child, rest, f);
1955	            }
1956	        }
1957	        Value::Array(items) if head == "*" => {
1958	            for item in items.iter_mut() {
1959	                for_each_at(item, rest, f);
1960	            }
1961	        }
1962	        _ => {}
1963	    }
1964	}

1966	/// Drop the index names this principal may not read, at the positions this
1967	/// endpoint actually carries them — and nowhere else.
1968	fn prune_json(v: &mut Value, sites: &[Site], principal: &Principal, known: &HashSet<String>) {
1969	    for site in sites {
1970	        match *site {
1971	            Site::KeyedByIndex(path) => for_each_at(v, path, &mut |node| {
1972	                if let Value::Object(map) = node {
1973	                    map.retain(|k, _| !hidden(k, principal, known));
1974	                }
1975	            }),
1976	            Site::NamedIn(path, field) => for_each_at(v, path, &mut |node| {
1977	                if let Value::Array(items) = node {
1978	                    items.retain(|item| match item {
1979	                        Value::String(s) => !hidden(s, principal, known),
1980	                        Value::Object(o) if !field.is_empty() => !o
1981	                            .get(field)
1982	                            .and_then(Value::as_str)
1983	                            .map(|n| hidden(n, principal, known))
1984	                            .unwrap_or(false),
1985	                        _ => true,
1986	                    });
1987	                }
1988	            }),
1989	        }
1990	    }
1991	}

1993	/// Line filter for `_cat` in its default text form: a row whose index column
1994	/// names a hidden index is dropped whole. A table with no index column
1995	/// (`columns` is empty) is returned untouched.
1996	fn prune_text(
1997	    bytes: &[u8],
1998	    columns: &[usize],
1999	    principal: &Principal,
2000	    known: &HashSet<String>,
2001	) -> Vec<u8> {
2002	    if columns.is_empty() {
2003	        return bytes.to_vec();
2004	    }
2005	    let Ok(text) = std::str::from_utf8(bytes) else {
2006	        return bytes.to_vec();
2007	    };
2008	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
2009	    let mut dropped_any = false;
2010	    for line in text.split_inclusive('\n') {
2011	        let fields: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
2012	        let hides = columns.iter().any(|&c| {
2013	            fields
2014	                .get(c)
2015	                .map(|token| {
2016	                    hidden(
2017	                        token.trim_matches(|ch: char| ch == '"' || ch == ','),
2018	                        principal,
2019	                        known,
2020	                    )
2021	                })
2022	                .unwrap_or(false)
2023	        });
2024	        if hides {
2025	            dropped_any = true;
2026	        } else {
2027	            out.push_str(line);
2028	        }
2029	    }
2030	    if dropped_any {
2031	        out.into_bytes()
2032	    } else {
2033	        bytes.to_vec()
2034	    }
2035	}

2836	    /// /_xerj/wal_tap` echoes `target_url`, and `GET /_xerj/wal_tap/_stats`

2838	    /// (`_xerj` has no `prune_sites` entry, and adding one would not help — a
2839	    /// scoped key has no business knowing the tap's target either). Both are

2886	    /// the engine expands a wildcard over the principal's visible set. Snapshot
2887	    /// and restore are the two verbs that never reach that funnel:
2888	    /// `Engine::create_snapshot` walks the index map itself, and
2889	    /// `Engine::restore_snapshot` expands the pattern against the snapshot's
2890	    /// own manifest and then removes and rewrites the index directory directly
2891	    /// — no `get_index`, no `delete_index`. A wildcard waved through here is a
2892	    /// wildcard executed, which made
2893	    /// `POST /_snapshot/{repo}/{snap}/_restore {"indices":".xerj-memory-*"}`
2894	    /// roll every tenant's brain back to the backup instant for any
2895	    /// authenticated caller, and `{"indices":"*"}` on the create side back up

2901	            &[".xerj-memory-alice-edges", ".xerj-memory-alice"],
2902	            &[Privilege::ReadIndex, Privilege::WriteIndex],
2903	        );

2905	
2906	        for body in [
2907	            r#"{"indices":".xerj-memory-*"}"#,
2908	            r#"{"indices":[".xerj-memory-*"]}"#,
2909	            r#"{"indices":"*"}"#,
2910	            r#"{"indices":["*"]}"#,
2911	            r#"{"indices":"_all"}"#,
2912	            r#"{"indices":"logs-*,.xerj-*"}"#,
2913	        ] {
2914	            for p in [&legacy, &alice, &logs] {
2915	                assert!(
2916	                    !check(p, Method::POST, "/_snapshot/repo/s1/_restore", body),
2917	                    "restore {body} destroys the reserved namespace and must be refused"
2918	                );
2919	                assert!(
2920	                    !check(p, Method::PUT, "/_snapshot/repo/s1", body),
2921	                    "snapshot {body} captures the reserved namespace and must be refused"
2922	                );
2923	            }

2925	
2926	        // A tenant still backs up and rolls back its OWN indices, by name …
2927	        assert!(check(
2928	            &alice,
2929	            Method::PUT,
2930	            "/_snapshot/repo/s1",
2931	            r#"{"indices":[".xerj-memory-alice"]}"#
2932	        ));

2934	            &alice,

2936	            "/_snapshot/repo/s1/_restore",

## FINDINGS (ranked)

### F1 — HIGH: Remote panic → process abort via multi-byte UTF-8 in a search sort `format` string
**File:** `/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-api/src/es_compat.rs`
**Panic site:** line 4136 `let rest = &fmt[i..];`, caused by lines 4186-4187:
```rust
} else {
    out.push(bytes[i] as char);   // mangles a multi-byte char, advances one BYTE
    i += 1;

```
`java_pattern_to_strftime` walks the pattern byte-wise; when it hits a non-ASCII character it pushes one byte as a char and advances `i` by 1, so the next iteration's `&fmt[i..]` slices mid-character → `byte index N is not a char boundary` panic. With `[profile.release] panic = "abort"` (engine/Cargo.toml:160-166), the whole process dies — not just the request task.

**Reachability (verified):** `search_impl` (line 9991) → hit serialization line 15146 `format_sort_value(raw, spec.and_then(|s| s.format.as_deref()))` → line 4113 `java_pattern_to_strftime(fmt)`. `SortField.format` is taken verbatim from the request body with no validation (`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-query/src/parser.rs:3309`: `let format = obj.get("format").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(String::from);`). The format arm only needs the sort value to be a `Value::Number`.

**Request shape** (index needs ≥1 doc with a numeric/date field `n`):
```

```
`中` = 3 bytes; iteration i=1 → `&fmt[1..]` panics. Any 2+ byte non-ASCII char outside a `'…'` quoted literal works (e.g. `"é"`).

**Privilege:** any principal that can issue a search — including a **share-link GUEST** (`_search` is in `GUEST_INDEX_OPS`, authz.rs:1408-1415, and `format` is not a denied shape), and unauthenticated callers when the node runs open mode (`--insecure`). This is the same defect class the repo already fixed three times in the date-math resolvers (#207, see comments at es_compat.rs:19482, 19503, 19522: "`+1中` / `/中` → byte index 1 is not a char boundary") — the fourth copy was missed here. Note the engine's own `java_to_strftime` (xerj-engine/src/aggs.rs:4870) is panic-free because it slices `bytes[i..]`, never `&str[i..]`.

### F2 — HIGH: Unbounded CPU (infinite loop) via `hdr.number_of_significant_value_digits` in a percentiles agg
**Files:**
- Primary: `/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-engine/src/aggs.rs:7856-7867` (`run_percentiles`, called unconditionally from the agg dispatcher at aggs.rs:2966)
- Second copy: `/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-api/src/es_compat.rs:6538-6549` (`hdr_percentiles_values`, reached at es_compat.rs:13006 whenever a hit has a negative value for the agg field)

```rust
let hdr_digits: u32 = params.get("hdr").and_then(|v| v.get("number_of_significant_value_digits"))
    .and_then(Value::as_u64).unwrap_or(3) as u32;      // unvalidated
let sub_bucket_count: u64 = {
    let target = 2u64 * 10u64.pow(hdr_digits);          // overflows for digits >= 20
    let mut p = 1u64;
    while p < target { p <<= 1; }                       // p wraps to 0 → never exits
    p
};
```
The parameter is never range-checked anywhere (grep finds only these two reads). Release builds have `overflow-checks off`, so `10u64.pow(d)` wraps mod 2^64. I computed the exact hanging values: **digits ∈ {20, 26, 29, 30, 31, 39, 41, 43, 46, 47, 48, 49, 52, 57, 58, 59}** produce a wrapped `target > 2^63`; `p` then walks 1,2,…,2^63 (all `< target`), the next `p <<= 1` wraps to 0, and `0 < target` loops forever — a pinned core and a request that never returns. (With overflow-checks on, `10u64.pow(20)` panics instead — equally fatal under `panic="abort"`.) ES restricts this parameter to 0-5; xerj accepts any u64.

**Request shape** (works even on an empty index — `sub_bucket_count` is computed before any doc access):
```
POST /logs/_search
{"size":0,"aggs":{"p":{"percentiles":{"field":"f","hdr":{"number_of_significant_value_digits":20}}}}}
```
**Privilege:** guest-sufficient (`_search`), same as F1.

## VERIFIED CLEAN (no findings)

- **Auth/authz parsing:** single consistent percent-decode between authz `segments()` and axum's `Path`; `IndexName::validate` (xerj-common/src/types.rs:100) blocks `/ \ .. NUL` and uppercase, and is enforced both at the es_compat `create_index` boundary (es_compat.rs:990) and in the engine; engine index lookups are in-memory DashMap hits (no path join on attacker names); reserved `.xerj-memory-*` namespace enforced by a task-local guard inside every engine index funnel, and guests are additionally limited to a strict route allow-list with `scroll`-param and PIT-in-body denials (authz.rs:1408-1507). No GUEST path to admin/write endpoints found.
- **`from`/`size` overflow → `merged_hits[start..end]` (12938/12951):** unreachable — every path (body field, `?size=`/`?from=` merged at 10100-10111, msearch sub-bodies at 25247) round-trips through `xerj_query::parse_request`'s `from.saturating_add(size) > MAX_RESULT_WINDOW (10_000)` clamp (xerj-query/src/parser.rs:269).
- **Body formats:** only JSON and NDJSON exist; Content-Type gate is `contains("json") || starts_with("text/plain")` else 415 (4032-4040). No msgpack/smile/yaml/CBOR parser anywhere.
- **Date-math index-name resolution (19374-19664):** all three historical defect copies are patched (ordering-checked brace slices, char-wise unit reads, `try_*`/`checked_*` duration math); `format_date` uses `str::replace` only.
- **Painless-lite `_update` script parser (19877-20149):** all byte walks are ASCII-delimiter anchored or `chars()`-based; no DSL injection (values become typed `serde_json::Value`s, paths become JSON keys).
- **EQL→DSL translation (43512-43672):** char-boundary-safe scanning; output built structurally via `serde_json::Map`, so predicates cannot inject DSL structure.
- **Other hand-rolled parsers checked and clean:** base64 decode/encode (37075-37130), murmur3 routing hash byte indexing (37529-37561), `_analyze` tokenizer (21118-21200, continuation bytes counted as in-token), glob matchers (16726-16788, 37714-37745), `parse_time_to_millis`/`parse_keep_alive_to_secs` (6045/37700, ASCII-suffix anchored, `saturating_mul`), `set/get/remove_dotted_path` (30246-30290, 37577-37615), mapping/`fields` walk slices (13674-14300 — all `ends_with`/`rfind('.')` anchored), msearch NDJSON loop bounds + per-item `parse_request` (25028-25382), scroll-id UUID gate (22664), `profile_shard_count` clamp + `Vec::with_capacity` (7281/16087), snapshot repo/snapshot name validators (32140+).
- **Headers:** `X-OpenSearch-Version`/`x-elastic-product` built only from config/constant strings via `HeaderValue::from_str` (router.rs:1065-1094) — no CRLF injection; no attacker-controlled response-header reflection found; `is_opensearch_caller`/`resolve_compat_version` only read `User-Agent` for a boolean. CORS defaults to emitting no ACAO.
- **Amplification:** gzip decompression is layered *outside* `RequestBodyLimitLayer` on both routers, so the limit bounds decompressed bytes; `/_share/claim` (the one unauthenticated body route) has its own small `DefaultBodyLimit`; no attacker-sized allocation found (`dense_vector` `dims` is stored unclamped at 18105 but I found no dims-sized allocation that doesn't also require an equally large ingested vector — not a verified finding).
- All ~55 production (non-test) `unwrap`/`expect` sites were individually traced and are guarded.

**Posture notes (design, not findings):** unscoped minted keys retain operator-level reach including `PUT /_snapshot/{repo}` with an arbitrary `settings.location`; open mode (`--insecure`) makes every caller Superuser by design.
